## What was observed

Two sub-agent sessions on #82 were asked to compare their own injected
context against the repository. They came out opposite ways, on the same
branch, hours apart:

| | injected `AGENTS.md` | injected own definition | injected `gitStatus` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verifier`, round 1 | stale (`be17114`, 15 commits back) | current | not checked |
| `code-review`, round 2 | stale (`be17114`) | current (contained #80's text) | stale: branch `main`, tip `be17114`, date three days off |
| `verifier`, round 4 | **current** (HEAD) | **stale** — byte-identical to `HEAD:.claude/agents/verifier.md`, missing the paragraph in the working tree it had been asked to verify | not checked |

The last row is the one that matters. #82's fix rests on the assumption
that a sub-agent's own definition is loaded fresh at invocation while
`AGENTS.md` is a session-start snapshot — that asymmetry is *why* the
clause was put in the definitions rather than in `AGENTS.md`. Round 4
shows the asymmetry does not hold in both directions: a definition is a
snapshot too, and it can be the stale one while `AGENTS.md` is current.

The fix still works — it is strictly better than nothing under either
mechanism, and a definition that is merely behind `HEAD` still carries
whatever rule was last committed. But the repository should not go on
believing the mechanism is what it is not.

## Two distinct gaps

**1. `gitStatus` can name the wrong branch.** A reviewer was told
`Current branch: main`, tip `be17114`, while the worktree was on
`docs/pointers-read-from-the-repo` three days later. It caught this only
because it was explicitly asked to measure its context. An agent that
trusts that block inspects the wrong branch and reports on the wrong
diff — and unlike a stale file, there is no fresher copy to be pointed
at, only `git` itself. None of the three definitions currently says to
re-derive branch and tip from `git` rather than reading the block.

**2. A definition can be stale.** Nothing follows from this for the
definition's own rules, but it does mean an uncommitted change to a
sub-agent's instructions is invisible to that sub-agent — including,
as in round 4, while it is verifying that very change. Worth knowing
before someone tries to test an agent definition by editing it and
invoking it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The definitions tell an agent to take branch and tip from `git`,
      not from the injected status block. One sentence, in the same
      shape as #82's clause.
- [ ] Somewhere durable records that a definition is also a snapshot, so
      the next person reasoning about #82's design does not repeat the
      assumption that only `AGENTS.md` goes stale.

Related: #82 (the clause), #84 (the pointer whose reader has no fresh
source), #81 (nothing checks the definitions at all). Follow the workflow
in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF

as good as the copy it consults. AGENTS.md reaches a session through
CLAUDE.md's import, as a snapshot, and the snapshot can be old: a
verifier checking this very rule found its copy fifteen commits behind
the file on disk, nine of them touching AGENTS.md, across three days --
with no trace of the section the claim it was checking pointed at. Its
negative control was `grep -c 'The review sub-agents'`: 0 in context, 1
on disk.

code-review.md's pointer now carries the clause ui-review.md got in #71,
byte for byte. verifier.md gets the general form, because the pass whose
job is checking claims reads more files than one: sst.doc, a test, a
source file a comment cites. Those reach a sub-agent quoted into its task
description from the main agent's memory of them, which the work under
verification may since have changed. A claim checked against a stale copy
can be marked wrong for agreeing with the current rule, or right for
agreeing with one that has been replaced.

The clause lives in the definitions rather than once in AGENTS.md because
a rule about stale copies of AGENTS.md cannot be stated only there. That
was the stated design, and it is now known to be shakier than it looked:
a later verifier round found its own definition stale while its AGENTS.md
was current -- the reverse combination. Filed as #85 rather than reopened
here, because it weakens the reason without weakening the fix. AGENTS.md
was the stale side in two of the three measured sessions; a definition
still carries whatever rule was last committed, and this is that commit.

code-review.md keeps the narrow wording while verifier.md generalizes.
That is a decision, not an oversight: #82 asks that its two named
definitions say it the same way, and broadening one would break the
byte-for-byte parity that satisfies the criterion. The residual exposure
is real -- code-review.md sends the reviewer to sst.doc twice -- and is
filed as #86.

Closes #82.

## The problem, demonstrated on itself

A pointer telling a sub-agent to consult a section of `AGENTS.md` is only
as good as the copy it consults. `AGENTS.md` reaches a session through
`CLAUDE.md`'s import, as a snapshot — and the snapshot can be old.

The `verifier` round on this branch measured its own context and found
that copy **fifteen commits behind** the file on disk, nine of them
touching `AGENTS.md`, across three days: 165 lines against 381, with no
`### The review sub-agents` section at all — the section that
`code-review.md`'s pointer names. Its negative control was
`grep -c 'The review sub-agents'`: **0** in context, **1** on disk. The
first `code-review` round reproduced it independently.

So the bug was live inside the sessions reviewing the fix.

## The change

- `.claude/agents/code-review.md` — the pointer gains the clause
  `ui-review.md` got in #71, byte for byte.
- `.claude/agents/verifier.md` — the general form, because the pass whose
  job is checking claims reads more files than one. `sst.doc`, a test, a
  source file a comment cites: those reach a sub-agent quoted into its
  task description from the main agent's memory of them, which the work
  under verification may since have changed.

The clause lives in the definitions rather than once in `AGENTS.md`
because a rule about stale copies of `AGENTS.md` cannot be stated only
there.

The design assumes definitions load fresh while `AGENTS.md` is a
snapshot. The third `verifier` round broke the assumption: its
`AGENTS.md` was **current at HEAD** while its own `verifier.md` was
byte-identical to committed HEAD and **missing the entire paragraph it
had been asked to verify**. Had it trusted its context it would have
reported the change as absent.

That weakens the stated reason without weakening the fix — `AGENTS.md`
was the stale side in two of the three measured sessions, and a stale
definition still carries whatever rule was last committed, which is what
this commit makes. Filed as #85 rather than reopened here.

## Decisions recorded

`code-review.md` keeps the narrow wording while `verifier.md`
generalizes. That is deliberate: #82's second acceptance criterion is
that its two named definitions say it the same way, and they now match
byte for byte from "from the file in the repository" through "which may
predate the rule". Broadening one would break the parity inside the slice
that established it. The residual exposure — `code-review.md` sends the
reviewer to `sst.doc` twice — is #86.

## Issues filed

- **#84** — `ui-review.md`'s frontmatter pointer, the one this cannot
  help: its reader is the main agent, which has no fresh source to be
  redirected to.
- **#85** — the injected snapshots go stale independently. Three
  sessions, three different combinations, including a `code-review` round
  whose `gitStatus` named the wrong branch while its `AGENTS.md` was
  current.
- **#86** — the residual generalization above.

Also corrected #84's body by comment: it had repeated the ambiguous
"nine commits" formulation this branch exists to fix.

`ui-review` **did not run and is not owed** — two agent definitions,
nothing compiled, no `sst.doc`, no `tests/`, no feature flag, no byte the
game prints. Both `code-review` rounds independently agreed.

days from `git`, hashed the shared clause span across all three
definitions (identical), confirmed `CLAUDE.md:6` is `@AGENTS.md`, ran

in a scratch tree and ran the full suite, **11/11 in 176s**, to confirm
the diff is inert. It reported one environment gap: `cppcheck`,
`clang-tidy` and `scan-build` are absent, with no C changed for them to
scan.

finding that "nine commits behind" reads ambiguously alone. It was
re-derived independently in `code-review` rather than by a fourth
verifier pass — three integers and a rewrap were its whole verifiable
surface, and the reviewer checked the rewrap for dropped and duplicated
fragments mechanically.

Below 72x24 the panels overlap instead of clipping, and now do it live
## Problem

`make_windows()` in `tui.c` says what it means to do when the terminal
falls below the 72x24 the display asks for:

> A terminal that has shrunk below the 72x24 the display asks for at
> startup is not torn down mid-game: the panels keep their size and the
> screen clips, which is ugly but leaves the player where they were.

What actually happens is not clipping. At 40x14 the status panel bleeds
through the quadrant box and the two interleave — `xorWarp Fact`,
`xLeTime Left`, `     7.00qj` — and the message window collapses to a
single row.

## Why it matters more now

Before #46 the mess appeared only after the player's next keystroke,
because the windows were rebuilt at the next prompt. The display now
follows the terminal while the player is still dragging, so a drag
through the minimum repaints the overlap repeatedly, live.

The garbling itself predates that change and reproduces on the commit
before it; what #46 changed is how often a player sees it.

## Suggested approach

Decide what sub-minimum should look like, since the comment's stated
intention and the behaviour disagree:

- draw a single "terminal too small" line and skip the panel repaint
  while `LINES < 24 || COLS < 72`, restoring the panels when there is
  room again; or
- genuinely clip — draw the panels only as far as the terminal reaches,
  which is what the comment promises.

The first is less w

content.text:
**#78.** It's the only open issue a player can actually run into, and #46 made it worse — the display now repaints while you drag, so shrinking past 72x24 garbles the panels live rather than at the next keystroke. The comment in `make_windows()` promises clipping and the code doesn't clip; that gap is the whole slice.

It also splits cleanly into a thin one: decide the sub-minimum behavior (a "terminal too small" line is the smaller change and the honest one, versus real clipping which is what the comment claims), implement, and cover it in `tests/tui.sh` at 40x14 — that file already drives tmux and is where 72x24/80x24 coverage lives. It's the first real `ui-review` binding change since #46, and the last four commits have all been instruction files.

The alternative worth naming is **#81** — nothing checks the agent definitions load or agree with `AGENTS.md`. Four commits have now edited those files on nothing but hand inspection, and #82's parity between the three clauses will drift silently the first time someone rewords one. It's the right follow-on to what just merged; it's just worth less than fixing something a player sees.

Say the word and I'll start #78 — beginning, per step 3, by checking the issue's premise that the garbling predates #46.

content.text:
Mechanism confirmed at 66x24: `"...2500.0 uni"` truncates and the overflow `ts` lands on the next row as `xtsKlingons Left 2`. That's `draw_status_line()` at `tui.c:108-118` — a `waddch` loop with no bounds check, so ncurses wraps the remainder onto the following row of `wstat`, clobbering its left border and padding, and on the last line its bottom border (`     7.00qj`).

The issue's premise is wrong in a way worth correcting: nothing overlaps. Let me confirm the scope before I write the test.

fails=0
fail() {
	printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2
	fails=$((fails + 1))
}

screen() { tm capture-pane -t "$pane" -p 2>/dev/null; }

# The same, with whatever has scrolled off. Only meaningful once the
# game has fallen back to the classic display: curses runs on the
# alternate screen, which keeps no history.
scrollback() { tm capture-pane -t "$pane" -p -S - 2>/dev/null; }

wait_scrollback() {
	i=0
	while [ "$i" -lt 80 ]; do
		if scrollback | grep -qF -- "$1"; then return 0; fi
		i=$((i + 1))
		sleep 0.1
	done
	return 1
}

dump() {
	printf '  --- screen ---\n' >&2
	screen | sed 's/^/  | /' >&2
}

# For failures where the evidence may be exactly what scrolled away.
dump_scrollback() {
	printf '  --- screen, with scrollback ---\n' >&2
	scrollback | sed 's/^/  | /' >&2
}

# Wait until the screen shows $1, up to about eight seconds. Polling
# beats a fixed sleep: curses paints in its own time, and a machine
# under load should not turn into a failure.
wait_for() {
	i=0
	while [ "$i" -lt 80 ]; do
		if screen | grep -qF -- "$1"; then return 0; fi
		i=$((i + 1))
		sleep 0.1
	done
	return 1
}

# Answer any paging prompts until the command prompt comes back. A
# space is only ever sent while a pause is actually showing, so this
# cannot quietly paper over a pause that should not have been there.
to_command() {
	i=0
	while [ "$i" -lt 40 ]; do
		screen | grep -qF 'COMMAND' && return 0
		if screen | grep -qE 'CONTINUE|HIT SPACE BAR'; then
			tm send-keys -t "$pane" Space
		fi
		i=$((i + 1))
		sleep 0.25
	done
	return 1
}

want() {
	screen | grep -qF -- "$2" || { fail "$1"; dump; }
}

# Like to_command, but reports in $saw whether $1 was on screen at any
# point along the way. For text meant to arrive and then scroll on:
# looking only once the prompt is back asks whether it is *still*

# --- a shrink with a conversation behind it ---------------------------
# " COMMAND> " is the most repeated string in the game, so deciding
# whether the live prompt survived a shrink by looking for that text
# finds an answered prompt further up instead. The cursor then sits in
# the middle of the history: the player types into a command they ran
# two turns ago, and the game reads a line that was never on screen.
#
# Needs a few commands behind it -- with an empty conversation there is
# no older prompt to match, which is why every earlier resize case here
# passes either way.
start 100 30 'tournament 7 short novice pw'
if ! to_command; then
	fail "shrink history: the game never reached its command prompt"
	dump
else
	for c in status damages; do
		tm send-keys -t "$pane" "$c" Enter
		sleep 0.5
	done
	tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 100 -y 24
	sleep 1
	tm send-keys -t "$pane" 'ch'
	sleep 0.5
	# What is typed has to be at the bottom, on a prompt of its own.
	if ! screen | grep -v '^ *$' | tail -1 | grep -qE 'COMMAND> *ch *$'; then
		fail "shrink history: typing after the shrink did not go to the live prompt"

# --- a shrink past the minimum clips instead of wrapping ---------------
# make_windows() promises that a terminal shrunk below the 72x24 the
# display asks for "keeps its size and the screen clips". It did not
# clip: draw_status_line() wrote the whole line a character at a time
# with nothing stopping it at the window edge, so curses wrapped what
# did not fit onto the next row of the same window -- over the left
# border and the padding column, and on the last line over the bottom
# border. At 40 columns that read as `xtsKlingons Left 2` and a bottom
# border of `     7.00qj`.
#
# 40 columns rather than 71: both wraps need the text to overrun, and
# "Time Left" is the shortest line there is, so the one that lands on
# the border only shows up well below the minimum.
start 100 30 'tournament 7 short novice pw'
if ! to_command; then
	fail "sub-minimum: the game never reached its command prompt"
	dump
else
	tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 40 -y 24
	sleep 1
	# The panels have to actually be there and actually be too narrow,
	# or everything below this passes by describing an empty screen.
	if ! screen | grep -qF 'Quadrant'; then
		fail "sub-minimum: the panels are not on screen to be checked"
		dump
	elif [ "$(screen | head -1 | wc -c)" -gt 45 ]; then
		fail "sub-minimum: the terminal did not shrink"
		dump
	elif screen | grep -qF '2500.0 units'; then
		fail "sub-minimum: the status lines still fit, so nothing was clipped"
		dump
	else
		# Column 30 is the status panel's left border: the quadrant box
		# is 29 wide, so its own border ends at 29. Every row of the
		# panels carries the same character there. Which character is
		# not the point -- capture-pane renders the line-drawing set as
		# it pleases -- but a row that disagrees with the others is text
		# that wrapped into the border.
		if ! screen | awk 'NR >= 2 && NR <= 12 { seen[substr($0, 30, 1)] = 1 }
		                   END { exit length(seen) == 1 ? 0 : 1 }'; then
			fail "sub-minimum: a status line wrapped over the panel border"
			dump
		fi
		# The bottom border of the panels is the row starting with the
		# bottom-left corner. Nothing numeric belongs on it: the only
		# caption it ever carries is SENSORS DAMAGED.
		if screen | awk '/^.[^ ]/ && substr($0,1,1) != " " { if (NR >= 12 && NR <= 14 && /[0-9]/ && !/Quadrant/) bad = 1 }
		                 END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }'; then
			:
		else
			fail "sub-minimum: a status line wrapped over the bottom border"
			dump
		fi
	fi
fi

Premise correction before building on this, per AGENTS.md step 3. The

**Nothing overlaps, and the quadrant box is not involved.** In
`xorWarp Fact` the leading `x` is the *quadrant* panel's own right
border, intact and in its correct column. What follows is the status
panel writing over **its own** left border and padding column.

**The cause is an unbounded draw, not a layout error.**
`draw_status_line()` (`tui.c:108-118`) walks the string with `waddch`
and nothing stops it at the window edge. `waddch` past the last column
wraps to the next row of the same window, so the tail of a line too long
to fit lands on the row below, on top of that row's border and padding —
and for the last line, on top of the bottom border, which is where
`     7.00qj` comes from. The layout is correct at every size; the
windows never overlap.

Clearest at 66x24, where exactly two characters overrun:

```
x  8  . . . . . . E . . .   xx Shields       DOWN, 100% 2500.0 uni
x  9  . . . . . . . . . .   xtsKlingons Left 2                   x
```

`ts` is the end of `units`, wrapped onto the next row.

**The trigger is the text not fitting, not the 72x24 threshold.** The
longest status line — `Shields       DOWN, 100% 2500.0 units` — is 37
columns, and the status panel gets `COLS - 29` less its borders. So it
garbles at 67 columns and below, and 71x24 renders cleanly. 68x24 is a
half-case: the text fits only by consuming the right border, which goes
missing on that row without wrapping.

Two claims in the body I checked and can confirm:

- The garbling predates #79 and reproduces on `dbcaa63`, the commit
  before it.
- #79 changed how often a player sees it. Verified by `SIGSTOP`ping the
  game before the drag: with the process stopped nothing appears, and
  the fragments arrive on `SIGCONT`. They are the game's own drawing,
  not a tmux reflow artifact.

**What this changes about the slice.** The two options in "Suggested
approach" were offered as a choice about what sub-minimum *should* look
like. With the cause understood, option 2 is not a policy choice but
the actual bug fix, and it is three lines: bound both draw loops to the
window's inner width. That makes the existing comment at `tui.c:128-132`
true as written — the panels keep their size and the screen clips — so
the disagreement the issue asks to resolve resolves in favour of the
code's stated intention.

Option 1 (a "terminal too small" notice replacing the panels) remains
available and is a genuine design question, but it is a separate,
larger change and no longer the only way to stop the garbling. Taking
option 2 unless you say otherwise; the acceptance criteria this issue
sets are untouched either way.

One thing option 2 does **not** address, which the body also mentions:
below 24 rows the message window still collapses toward a single row
(`msgh = LINES - PANELH`). That is real, separate, and not part of this
slice.

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c`, `draw_status_line()`. Widths from 47 to 71 columns (room 15-39) leave part of a value on screen. Driven live, with the true values in parentheses:

- 49 cols: `Energy        367` (3675.25) — reads as a ship about to die

- 54 cols: `Shields       DOWN, 10` (100%)
- 53 cols: `Shields       DOWN, 1`

Suggestion, three lines and no new screen: in `draw_status_line()`, when `(int)strlen(s) > room && room > 0`, stop at `room-1` and write a marker (`>`) in the last cell — `Energy        36>` cannot be misread, and a player learns in one glance that the panel is cut rather than the ship is dying. It also buys back the zero slack at the supported minimum: the longest line is 40 against a room of 40 today, so any future word added to a status line would silently lose its tail at 72x24 instead of visibly wrapping. Applying the same to `draw_quad_line()` costs nothing and keeps the two loops symmetrical.

**should-fix (small) — the ` Status ` box title still wraps over the panel's own left border**
`tui.c:477` (`mvwaddstr(wstat, 0, 2, " Status ")`) is not clipped, and the title is 8 columns. At 33-36 columns the status window is 4-7 wide, so the title wraps to row 1 and lands on the border column:


`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:16-21` says "Resizing the terminal is fine at any point. The display follows it straight away… both the question you were asked and the answer you were halfway through typing survive." Worth filing; it is the far end of the very journey this slice is about.

**coverage nit (candidate issue)** — nothing pins the invariant the "no change at legal sizes" claim depends on. `tests/test_tuifmt.c` never asserts that any `fmt_status_line()` output fits `72 - QUADW - 3 = 40` columns. A one-line check over the states it already builds would keep a future word added to the Shields or Life Support line from silently truncating at the minimum supported size.

# Super Star Trek

Super Star Trek is an old text-only game, an early example of a turn-based space strategy sim, written in BASIC. In this game, you are the captain of the starship Enterprise, and your mission is to scout the federation space and eliminate all the invading Klingon ships. You will have to manage the ship energy carefully, use phasers and torpedoes to destroy the Klingons, and find starbases to repair damages and replenish your energy. All of this, rendered with a few characters on screen and a lot of imagination.

Super Star Trek is probably the most famous early text-only game ever created and it inspired many other videogames. Since the code was public domain, during the years, it was changed and improved many times. There are literally thousands of versions out there. All of them are nice, but my preference goes to the classic 1978 version called Super Star Trek.

[Read more about Star Trek and Super Star Trek.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Trek_%281971_video_game%29)

### Full-screen mode

Run `sst -t` for a full-screen interface: the short-range scan and the
ship's status stay on screen in two panels while the usual game
conversation scrolls below them. It needs a terminal of at least 72x24
and can be combined with the fixed-coordinate option (`sst -f -t`).
Without `-t` the game uses its classic scrolling display.

Resizing the terminal is fine at any point. The display follows it
straight away — while the game is waiting for you to answer, and while
it is waiting for a keystroke at a pause — and both the question you
were asked and the answer you were halfway through typing survive.
Older text that no longer fits scrolls away, as it would in any
terminal.

If full-screen mode isn't possible — the terminal is too small, the
game isn't attached to one (piped input, redirected output, a job with
no tty), or `TERM` names a terminal that can't address the cursor —
`-t` prints a notice and plays in the classic display instead.

### Building

The build is CMake, and a build type is required:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug   # or Release
cmake --build build
./build/sst
```

You need a C17 compiler and ncurses (`libncurses-dev` on Debian and
Ubuntu; already present on macOS). `ctest --test-dir build` runs the
test suite, which includes a full-screen session driven through a real
terminal and needs `tmux` — without it that one test reports as skipped.

### Windows

There is no working Windows build at the moment.

The old instructions here were `cl /DWINDOWS /Fesst.exe *.c` from a
Visual Studio Developer Command Prompt. That has not worked for some
time: `tui.c` includes `<curses.h>` unconditionally, and `sst.c`,
`finish.c` and `osx.c` all call into it, so the full-screen display
cannot simply be left out of the file list either.

Making it work again means stubbing the display out under `#ifdef
WINDOWS` — `tui_init()` returning false, so the game always runs in its
classic scrolling form — and then actually building it on Windows to
find out what else has drifted. Nobody has a toolchain in play to check
that, so rather than leave instructions that fail, this says so.

## Problem

Drag a full-screen game (`sst -t`) below the panel geometry — under 29
columns or under 13 rows — and back up to 80x24, and the display does not
come back. The quadrant panel loses its right border, a full-width box
frames the message area, and the conversation and the `COMMAND>` prompt
are gone.

The process is alive and still reading input. The player sees a frozen
empty box with no way to tell that typing would work.

## Why

`make_windows()` (`tui.c`) creates `wquad` with `newwin(PANELH, QUADW, 0,
0)` and never resizes it — `wresize` is called on `wstat` and `wmsg`
only. When the terminal goes under the window's own size, ncurses'
automatic `resizeterm` stretches `wquad` to fit the screen, and nothing
puts it back afterwards.

## How to see it

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch new-session -d -x 80 -y 24 -s t './build/sst -t'
# answer the setup questions, get to COMMAND>
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch resize-window -t t -x 20 -y 10
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch resize-window -t t -x 80 -y 24
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch capture-pane -t t -p
```

Use your own socket (`-L`) as above, never the default one, and never a
bare `tmux kill-server`.

## Scope

Pre-existing. Found by `ui-review` on the branch for #78 and reproduced
identically on a build of that branch's merge-base, so the clipping fix
neither causes nor addresses it — #78 makes the panels clip cleanly at
every width down to the geometry, and this is what happens past it.

Related: #78 also notes the message window collapsing toward one row
below 24 rows (`msgh = LINES - PANELH`), which is the same class of
problem and equally unfixed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Shrinking to any size and growing back restores a working display.
- [ ] Covered in `tests/tui.sh`, which already drives resizes through a
      real pty.

Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
)"
gh issue create --title "Nothing pins that a status line fits the panel at the 72-column minimum" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Gap

`tests/test_tuifmt.c` checks that `fmt_status_line()` mirrors `srscan()`,
but never checks how wide its output is. The widest line the game can
produce is `Shields       DAMAGED, 100% 2500.0 units` at 40 columns,
against exactly 40 columns of room in the status panel at the 72-column
minimum — `COLS - QUADW` less the two borders and the two-column indent.

Zero slack, and nothing asserts it.

## Why it matters

Before #78 an over-long line wrapped onto the next row and wrecked the
panel border, which at least announced itself. After #78 the panels clip:
the line is cut and the last column becomes `>`. That is the right
behavior for a terminal a player has dragged too small, but at the
*supported minimum* it would be a silent defect — a status field losing
its tail on a size the game advertises as fine, visible only to whoever
happens to play at 72 columns with shields damaged.

Adding one word to a status label or one digit to a value is enough to
cross it, and #78's claim that "at the minimum and above nothing changes"
would quietly stop being true.

## Suggested approach

A check over the states `test_tuifmt.c` already builds: for every status
line in each, assert `strlen(buf) <= 72 - QUADW - 3`. `QUADW` is private
to `tui.c`, so either expose the room as a small helper or state the
number with a comment tying it to the minimum.

Worth covering the quadrant panel the same way while there — 26 columns
of room against a 24-column maximum line, which has slack but no test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test fails if any status line exceeds the room the panel has at
      72 columns.
- [ ] It is proven able to fail, per AGENTS.md step 4.

Found by `ui-review` on the branch for #78. Follow the workflow in
[AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF

content.text:
## Verdict

Acceptable as-is. All three fixes land well: the `>` marker reads unmistakably as "there is more to the right" (it is also what `less -S` uses for exactly this, so it is idiomatic rather than novel), it never appears on a line that fits, so it does not degrade into decoration; the captionless status box at 33-39 columns reads as squeezed rather than broken, especially with the quadrant box beside it still captioned; and the worst-case `Shields       DAMAGED, 100% 2500.0 units` line does fit at 72x24 with zero slack and no marker, which I checked on screen rather than by arithmetic. The full `tests/tui.sh` suite passes and plain mode is untouched. My findings are three nits, one of them a factual correction to the reasoning I was asked to verify: the quadrant title's exemption is not sound — `resize_term()` does shrink that window, and the title wraps over its own left border at 17 columns and below.

## Findings

**1. (nit, but the stated premise is wrong) The quadrant title wraps over its own border below 18 columns — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:495-505`**

The comment justifies leaving `" Quadrant %d - %d "` unguarded with "that window is a fixed 29 columns however small the terminal gets". It is not fixed: `sync_size()` calls `resize_term(0, 0)`, and ncurses shrinks every window that no longer fits the screen, `wquad` included. That is directly observable — at 25 and 20 columns the *grid* lines themselves clip and carry `>` markers, which can only happen if `panel_room(wquad)` has fallen below 26. The title then wraps at 17 and below, exactly the fault the `" Status "` guard removes:

```
=== 16 ===              === 12 ===
lq Quadrant 3 -         lq Quadrant
2     1 2 3 4 >x        3     1 2 >x
```

The stray `2` / `3` is the tail of the title sitting where the left border should be. A player only meets this at widths where the game is unplayable anyway (#88 territory), so the severity is low — but the reasoning in the comment is what a future maintainer will trust, and it is false. Suggestion: apply the same guard (`if (panel_room(wquad) >= (int)strlen(" Quadrant 8 - 8 "))` around the `mvwaddstr`/`mvwprintw` pair) and replace the justification with the real one, or, if it is judged out of scope, correct the comment to say the window *is* resized and the wrap is left to #88.

**2. (nit) The comment's threshold for dropping `" Status "` is off by four columns — same file, same comment block**

It says "below about 36 columns the status window is narrower than the title". The guard is `panel_room(wstat) >= 8`, i.e. `statw >= 11`, i.e. `COLS >= 40`. Observed: caption present at exactly 40, absent at 39 and 38. Suggestion: say 40, since that is the number someone reproducing this will type into `resize-window`.

**3. (nit) README over-promises the grow-back — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:24-27`**

"…and widening the terminal brings the rest straight back." True of the panels, which redraw from game state. Not true of the conversation immediately below them: narrowing to 40 and widening back leaves the briefing permanently cut (`your mission.  As you proceed you may`), and a narrow window can carry stray characters from the wider text until the next repaint. The paragraph's subject is the panels, so it is defensible, but it sits two paragraphs after one that promises the question and half-typed answer survive a resize, and a player will read the two together. Suggestion: "…and widening the terminal brings the panels straight back", which costs one word and removes the reading.

**Observation (no action suggested).** Below about 46 columns the status panel loses all of its alert colouring, because the coloured region begins at column 14 (`STATLABEL`) and is clipped away before the loop reaches it — a DAMAGED shields line at 45 columns renders as a plain `Shields     >`. That is a consequence of the pre-existing "colour the value, not the label" design rather than of this change, the marker tells the player how to get it back, and colouring a label whose value is not shown would arguably be worse. Noting it only because it is the one piece of information that silently disappears rather than visibly truncating.

**Confirmations requested.** (a) `Shields       DAMAGED, 100% 2500.0 units` at 72x24 ends flush against the right border with no marker — exact fit, zero slack, as #89 says; at 71 columns it clips and gains a `>`, which is the intended side of the line. (b) On the coloured case, the `>` on a clipped `Shields  DAMAGED, 100%>` does take the value's bold red. It reads as part of the value rather than as an independent alarm, and I would leave it. (c) `>` on a label (`Klingons Lef>`) and on a value (`Energy      >`) both read as "cut off"; the 33-column column-of-`>` is legible as a gutter meaning "widen me" and is a clear improvement on the truncated labels. (d) `>` never collides with a grid symbol, and the game's own `>` prompt lives only in the message window.

**Pre-existing, hit as expected.** #88 twice: shrinking to 80x10 spills a grid row over the bottom border (`mq 8  . . . . . . . . . * 9 .x`) and growing back to 80x24 leaves the quadrant box with no bottom border; and after any excursion below 29 columns, growing back leaves `wquad` one column wider than 29, so its right border overlaps the status panel's left border for the rest of the session. The second one is horizontal and happens from ordinary widths like 40 *after* a narrow excursion, which #88's "~20x10" wording may not cover — worth adding to that issue as evidence. I did not act on either.

## What I exercised

All via tmux on my own socket (`-f /dev/null -L uirev2`), cleaned up with `kill-server` on that socket only; no files modified.

- Read `AGENTS.md` (TUI rules), the full working-tree diff, `tui.c` (`make_windows`, `sync_size`, `tui_refresh_panels`, both draw loops), `tuifmt.c` (to bound the longest possible status line), `README.md` and `sst.doc:1541-1550`.

Acceptable as-is. The full `tests/tui.sh` suite passes and plain mode is untouched. My findings are three nits, one of them a factual correction to the reasoning I was asked to verify: the quadrant title's exemption is not sound — `resize_term()` does shrink that window, and the title wraps over its own left border at 17 columns and below.

## Findings

**1. (nit, but the stated premise is wrong) The quadrant title wraps over its own border below 18 columns — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:495-505`**

The comment justifies leaving `" Quadrant %d - %d "` unguarded with "that window is a fixed 29 columns however small the terminal gets". It is not fixed: `sync_size()` calls `resize_term(0, 0)`, and ncurses shrinks every window that no longer fits the screen, `wquad` included. That is directly observable — at 25 and 20 columns the *grid* lines themselves clip and carry `>` markers, which can only happen if `panel_room(wquad)` has fallen below 26. The title then wraps at 17 and below, exactly the fault the `" Status "` guard removes:

```
=== 16 ===              === 12 ===
lq Quadrant 3 -         lq Quadrant
2     1 2 3 4 >x        3     1 2 >x
```

The stray `2` / `3` is the tail of the title sitting where the left border should be. A player only meets this at widths where the game is unplayable anyway (#88 territory), so the severity is low — but the reasoning in the comment is what a future maintainer will trust, and it is false. Suggestion: apply the same guard (`if (panel_room(wquad) >= (int)strlen(" Quadrant 8 - 8 "))` around the `mvwaddstr`/`mvwprintw` pair) and replace the justification with the real one, or, if it is judged out of scope, correct the comment to say the window *is* resized and the wrap is left to #88.

**2. (nit) The comment's threshold for dropping `" Status "` is off by four columns — same file, same comment block**

It says "below about 36 columns the status window is narrower than the title". The guard is `panel_room(wstat) >= 8`, i.e. `statw >= 11`, i.e. `COLS >= 40`. Observed: caption present at exactly 40, absent at 39 and 38. Suggestion: say 40, since that is the number someone reproducing this will type into `resize-window`.

**3. (nit) README over-promises the grow-back — `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:24-27`**

"…and widening the terminal brings the rest straight back." True of the panels, which redraw from game state. Not true of the conversation immediately below them: narrowing to 40 and widening back leaves the briefing permanently cut (`your mission.  As you proceed you may`), and a narrow window can carry stray characters from the wider text until the next repaint. The paragraph's subject is the panels, so it is defensible, but it sits two paragraphs after one that promises the question and half-typed answer survive a resize, and a player will read the two together. Suggestion: "…and widening the terminal brings the panels straight back", which costs one word and removes the reading.

**Observation (no action suggested).** Below about 46 columns the status panel loses all of its alert colouring, because the coloured region begins at column 14 (`STATLABEL`) and is clipped away before the loop reaches it — a DAMAGED shields line at 45 columns renders as a plain `Shields     >`. That is a consequence of the pre-existing "colour the value, not the label" design rather than of this change, the marker tells the player how to get it back, and colouring a label whose value is not shown would arguably be worse. Noting it only because it is the one piece of information that silently disappears rather than visibly truncating.

# --- a shrink past the minimum clips instead of wrapping ---------------
# make_windows() promises that a terminal shrunk below the 72x24 the
# display asks for "keeps its size and the screen clips". It did not
# clip: draw_status_line() wrote the whole line a character at a time
# with nothing stopping it at the window edge, so curses wrapped what
# did not fit onto the next row of the same window -- over the left
# border and the padding column, and on the last line over the bottom
# border. At 40 columns that read as `xtsKlingons Left 2` and a bottom
# border of `     7.00qj`.
#
# 40 columns rather than 71: both wraps need the text to overrun, and
# "Time Left" is the shortest line there is, so the one that lands on
# the border only shows up well below the minimum.
start 100 30 'tournament 7 short novice pw'
if ! to_command; then
	fail "sub-minimum: the game never reached its command prompt"
	dump
else
	tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 40 -y 24
	sleep 1
	# The panels have to actually be there and actually be too narrow,
	# or everything below this passes by describing an empty screen.
	if ! screen | grep -qF 'Quadrant'; then
		fail "sub-minimum: the panels are not on screen to be checked"
		dump
	elif [ "$(screen | head -1 | wc -c)" -gt 45 ]; then
		fail "sub-minimum: the terminal did not shrink"
		dump
	elif screen | grep -qF '2500.0 units'; then
		fail "sub-minimum: the status lines still fit, so nothing was clipped"
		dump
	else
		# Column 30 is the status panel's left border: the quadrant box
		# is 29 wide, so its own border ends at 29. Every row of the
		# panels carries the same character there. Which character is
		# not the point -- capture-pane renders the line-drawing set as
		# it pleases -- but a row that disagrees with the others is text
		# that wrapped into the border.
		if ! screen | awk 'NR >= 2 && NR <= 12 { seen[substr($0, 30, 1)] = 1 }
		                   END { exit length(seen) == 1 ? 0 : 1 }'; then
			fail "sub-minimum: a status line wrapped over the panel border"
			dump
		fi
		# Row 13 is the panels' bottom border -- they are PANELH rows
		# deep and start at the top of the screen. Nothing numeric
		# belongs on it: the only caption it ever carries is SENSORS
		# DAMAGED.
		if ! screen | awk 'NR == 13 && /[0-9]/ { bad = 1 }
		                   END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }'; then
			fail "sub-minimum: a status line wrapped over the bottom border"
			dump
		fi
	fi
fi

	                     END { exit length(seen) == 1 ? 0 : 1 }'; then
		fail "sub-minimum: the panel title wrapped over the panel border"

fi

## Why

`make_windows()` (`tui.c`) lays the message window out as
`newwin(msgh, COLS-2, PANELH, 1)` — inset one column on the left, and
therefore ending one column short on the right. Nothing draws column 0
or the last column, so after a shrink whatever the terminal had there
stays until something else happens to overwrite it. The panels above are
unaffected because they span the full width between them.

Pre-existing, and not what #88 covers. #88 is about shrinking under the
panels' own geometry — below 29 columns or 13 rows — where `wquad` is
resized and never restored. This happens at 41x24, comfortably inside
that geometry, with all three windows the size they should be.

merge-base, so the clipping fix neither causes nor addresses it.

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch new-session -d -x 100 -y 30 -s t './build/sst -t'
# answer the setup questions, get to COMMAND>
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch resize-window -t t -x 41 -y 24
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch capture-pane -t t -p
```

Your own socket (`-L`) as above, never the default one, and never a bare
`tmux kill-server`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No column of the screen keeps text from a previous size.
- [ ] Covered in `tests/tui.sh`.

gives the conversation a left margin under the panels — so the fix is

```
=== 16 ===   mq SENSORS DAMAG         <- corner gone, caption runs into the border
```

- The precondition guard rewrite (both captions on row 1) is a real fix, not a formality — I confirmed the top row at 40 columns reads `lq Quadrant 3 - 2 qqqqqqqqqqklq Status k`, which the plain-mode prose cannot produce.
- I hit the missing `wquad` right border myself while testing and confirmed it is #88's stretched-window bug, unchanged by this diff.

### Review coverage

Your disclosure is specific enough to check, and I checked it. I agree that nothing changed after the last `ui-review` round reaches a screen: comment text in `tui.c`, prose in `README.md` and `tests/tui.sh` cannot alter what the game draws, and the only executable change was in the test script. No further round is owed **for the state as it stands**. Two consequences if you take the findings above: fixing (1) does change what the game draws below 20 columns, which puts step 6's rerun rule back in play; and the `verifier` owes a run either way, since it has not seen the three post-verifier fixes, let alone anything from this review.

Not a dodge on `draw_quad_line`'s clip: it only engages below 29 columns, and I confirmed by hand that the panels there are drawn correctly but do not survive being widened again (#88). Deferring it to a note on #88 is the right call. What I would not accept as a companion to it is finding (2), which needs no such preconditions — 16x24 renders cleanly on the fixed build and visibly wraps on the mutant.

### Could not review

- Static analysis: `cppcheck`, `clang-tidy`, `scan-build`, `shellcheck` and `valgrind` are all absent here, as the verifier reported. `shellcheck` is the one I would have wanted for the awk/quoting in the new test section.
- macOS behavior. Finding (4) rests on reading the awk source lineage, not on running it — I have no BSD awk here. If you can confirm `length(arr)` works on macOS's `/usr/bin/awk`, drop that nit.

## 1. Verdict

**Fail** — one blocking finding, in `README.md`. Everything else passed, and the mutation evidence held up under independent rebuild.

## 2. Failures

### F1 (deterministic, blocking): the README's row threshold is still off by one

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/README.md:28-30`:

> Squeezed **under about thirty columns or thirteen rows** the display does not recover on its own; quitting and starting again is the way back.

The columns half is right. The rows half is not: **thirteen rows does not recover either.** Measured by shrinking a live session and growing back to 100x30, 3/3 runs each:

```
100x14 -> 100x30: RECOVERED
100x13 -> 100x30: NOT recovered
100x12 -> 100x30: NOT recovered
100x29 wide -> ...: (columns) 30 RECOVERED, 29 NOT recovered
```

The 13-row wreck, after growing back to 100x30:

```
12  x 10  . . . . . . . . . .   xx Time Left     7.00      x
13  x                           xmqqqqqq...qqqqqqj      <- quadrant box has no bottom border
14  x                           x
15  x                           x                       <- and runs on down the screen
```

versus 14 rows, which comes back clean (`mqqq...j` on row 13, `COMMAND>` on 14). The mechanism: at `LINES == PANELH` the message window has no rows left (`tui.c:172`, `msgh = LINES-PANELH > 1 ? LINES-PANELH : 1`), so the display needs `PANELH + 1 == 14` rows intact, not `PANELH == 13`. The correction from twelve to thirteen moved in the right direction but stopped one short — "under fourteen rows", or "at or under thirteen rows", is what the measurement supports.

This matters because a player at exactly 13 rows reads that sentence, concludes widening will work, and it will not. It is in the diff, so it is this slice's to fix rather than #88's — #88 is the bug; this is the sentence describing where the bug starts.

Reproduce: `/tmp/.../scratchpad/recover2.sh <sst> <srcdir> 100 13` then inspect row 13 of the capture.

### No other failures

Nothing else failed, at any point, in any run.

## 3. What I checked hardest, and what I found

### 3.1 The mutation evidence — rebuilt independently, all five

I did not take the claim on trust. I rebuilt all five mutants myself in fresh copies outside the repository (`rsync` of the current working tree minus `.git` and `build*`, then a fresh `cmake -S <copy> -B <copy>/build`). I confirmed each one actually compiled its own sources by reading `build/CMakeFiles/sst.dir/tui.c.o.d`, which names the copy's `tui.c` in every case — the `AGENTS.md` cache-path trap is not in play. Each was run as `sh <copy>/tests/tui.sh <copy>/build/sst Debug`.

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| in-game quadrant title guard → `if (1)` | **1 FAIL**: `sub-minimum: the quadrant title wrapped over the panel border` |
| caption guard removed (`if (sensors_masked())` only) | **1 FAIL**: `sensors: the caption overran the box it captions` |
| `clip_at` → `return s[i]` (no marker) | **1 FAIL**: `sub-minimum: a clipped status line does not say it was clipped` |
| status title guard → `if (1)` | **1 FAIL**: `sub-minimum: the status title wrapped over the panel border` |
| `draw_status_line`'s `room = 10000` (the original bug) | **4 FAILs**, exactly the four reported |

Each fails exactly its own assertion and no other — no collateral, no cross-talk.

**The failure modes are the real ones**, not incidental. Quadrant title mutant, row 2 of the dump shows the wrapped remainder sitting on the left border where `x` belongs:

```
lq Quadrant 3 -
2     1 2 3 4 >x      <- "2 " is the tail of " Quadrant 3 - 2 ", on the border
x  1  . . . . >x
```

Caption mutant, row 13 — the bottom-right corner `j` eaten:

```
mq SENSORS DAMAGED       <- corner gone, string runs to the last column
```

**On the shared-source trap.** The two assertions you asked about are clean. The quadrant-title one asserts border-column uniformity read off the rendered pane — a structural property of the screen, with no path back to `panel_room` or to `strlen(" Quadrant 8 - 8 ")`. The caption one compares against a literal string and a literal width in the test file. Neither expectation descends from the code it checks.

**And I checked the guards against something independent of both** — the actual boundary, measured by shrinking a live session one column at a time:

```
caption:              20 cols -> "mq SENSORS DAMAGED j"   19 cols -> "mqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqj"
" Status ":           40 cols -> "...lq Status k"         39 cols -> "...lqqqqqqqqk"
" Quadrant 8 - 8 ":   19 cols -> "lq Quadrant 3 - 2 k"    18 cols -> "lq Quadrant qqqqqk"
bare " Quadrant ":    13 cols -> "lq Quadrant k"          12 cols -> "lqqqqqqqqqqk"
```

Every threshold in the corrected `tui.c:499-511` comment — 40, 19, 13, 20 — is exactly right, and at each boundary the heading fits with the corner intact and zero slack. The guards are neither too lenient nor too strict by even one column.

### 3.2 `uniform_col`

- **It can fail, and fails on a genuinely non-uniform column.** Proven live by two mutants, and synthetically: a row disagreeing at the column → exit 1; a single blank row among bordered rows → exit 1.
- **The `n > 0` guard means what you think, for the case you named.** Zero matched rows is a failure: an entirely empty capture → exit 1; a capture with fewer lines than `lo` → exit 1. Confirmed directly.
- **But it does not cover the case next door, and that is worth knowing.** `substr($0, col, 1)` returns `""` for a row shorter than the column. If *every* row in the range is shorter, all eleven agree on `""`, `n` is 11, and it **passes**:

  ```
  rows exist but all shorter than col 99 -> exit=0
  ```

  `capture-pane -p` strips trailing whitespace, so blank panel rows come back as empty lines — which is exactly the shape of a screen where the panels failed to draw. So `n > 0` rules out "no capture" but not "capture of nothing".

But per `AGENTS.md` step 4's last bullet it is the shape that goes quiet the day the data stops providing the case.

- Minor: it is load-bearing for **three** assertions, not four (`tests/tui.sh:829, 865, 894`).

I probed harder than last time and could not make it flake. Measured repaint latency after `resize-window`, polling at 10 ms:

| Condition | Latency |
|---|---|
| Unloaded | 14-19 ms |
| 96 spinners across 24 cores (loadavg ~10) | 41-133 ms |
| Pinned to one CPU, 8 spinners on it | 203-312 ms |
| Pinned to one CPU, 64 spinners on it | 1794-2493 ms |

The last row looks alarming but overstates the case: my poller forks a `capture-pane` every 10 ms and was competing for the same saturated core. So I replicated the real pattern instead — `resize; sleep 1; capture once` — which costs no CPU during the wait:

```
single CPU, 64 spinners:   0 miss of 30
single CPU, 300 spinners (loadavg 69):  0 miss of 30
```

Zero misses. The redraw is driven by `wgetch` returning `KEY_RESIZE` while the game is blocked at the prompt (`tui.c:612, 707`), so it needs one scheduling slice inside a whole second of wall clock, and the sleep itself is free. Full `tui.sh` runs under 96 spinners passed 3/3 (2x Debug, 1x Release).

**My recommendation: leave it.** Making it a polling wait would mean a `wait_for`-style helper that polls for a *width-dependent* condition, and there is no single string that works across 40/33/80/16/19 — each resize would need its own predicate, and at 16 and 19 columns the interesting predicate is a *negative* (the caption is gone), which cannot be polled for at all without a timeout that is itself a fixed sleep. It would add fragility to buy margin the measurements say is not needed. `sleep 1` is also already the file's idiom for this (12 occurrences, 6 of them pre-existing).
```sh
elif screen | awk 'NR >= 2 && NR <= 12 && /></ { bad = 1 }
```

awk lexes `/></` as the regex literal `><` (the two slashes are the delimiters). Nothing the panels draw ever contains `><`, so `bad` is never set, awk always exits 0, and the `elif` always takes the `:` branch. `"sub-minimum: a clip marker survived the widening"` is unreachable.

Demonstrated on the real thing, using the exact expression from the test against a captured 40-column screen whose every status line ends in `>`:

```
=== awk '></' test on this screen:   bad=0
=== awk '>' test:                    bad=1
```

Failure scenario: a regression where widening no longer repaints the panels (the `sync_size()`/`make_windows()` path, or a future change to `restore_curline()`'s guard) leaves ten `>` markers on a full-width screen and this section still reports OK. That is the one assertion behind the README's "widening the terminal brings the panels straight back", and behind your summary line "Grow-back is asserted at 80x24" — it currently asserts only that the panels are not showing literal `><`.

Fix: `/>/`. I verified the corrected form is not a false positive — on a recovered 80x24 in-game screen, rows 2-12 contain no `>` at all (`bad=0`), and on the 40-column screen it reports `bad=1`. While you are there, the `elif ... then : else fail` inversion reads backwards; `if screen | awk ... ; then` … `else fail` (or negating the pipeline) would match the shape of the two checks above it.

Note this also makes the rerun question moot: fixing it changes `tests/tui.sh`, so `verifier` owes another round regardless. On your own question — the three test hardenings *were* verifier findings, and step 7 says to rerun after addressing one; I'd have asked for that round anyway rather than take your own re-run of the suite in its place. `ui-review` is fine: the two changes since its third round are a README clause and a test comment, neither of which the game draws, so that round did see the player-facing state being committed.

### Nit

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:91-92` — the comment's arithmetic gives `W-4`, the code returns `W-3`.**
"the window less its two borders, less the two-column indent the text is drawn at" double-counts the left border: the two-column indent *is* the left border plus one padding column. The number is right (text occupies columns 2..`getmaxx-2`, which is `getmaxx-3` columns); the sentence is what a maintainer will check the code against, and it says the code is off by one. Suggest "the window less its right border, less the two columns the text is indented by".

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:506` — "the bare `" Quadrant "` that stands in before a game" misdescribes what happens in a game between 13 and 18 columns.**

As written, the comment tells a reader that below 19 an in-game panel has no caption, and the "a box with no caption is the better of the two" sentence that follows reinforces the wrong reading. Suggest: "…the bare `" Quadrant "` that stands in before a game — and inside one wherever the coordinates no longer fit — below 13".

**`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tests/tui.sh:119-128` — `uniform_col`'s contract is stated at one call site instead of at the definition.**
You asked directly. The definition comment says only "every row … carries the same character", which is true and complete-sounding; the trap — rows shorter than the column all read empty, agree with each other, and pass — is documented at `tests/tui.sh:895-898`, in front of the third of three call sites. The `n > 0` guard in the code rules out "no capture at all", not "capture of nothing", and nothing at the definition says so. One sentence there ("a screen whose rows are all shorter than column `$1` agrees with itself and passes, so prove the panels are drawn before asking") makes the next call site safe by default rather than by whoever writes it remembering. Keep the call-site note too; it is doing different work.

## Your other questions

- **Are the four guards consistent with each other and with the comment?** Yes. `" Quadrant "` 10 → width 13, `" Status "` 8 → wstat width 11 → COLS 40, `" Quadrant 8 - 8 "` 16 → width 19, `" SENSORS DAMAGED "` 17 → width 20; every threshold in the comment matches, and I confirmed all four on screen (at 19 the in-game title fills exactly to the corner; at 16 the bare label appears; at 40 the status title is the last width it survives). The `" Quadrant 8 - 8 "` literal is a true width, not an upper bound — `quadx`/`quady` are galaxy coordinates 1-8 everywhere they are assigned. `clip_at`'s `s[i+1]` read is in bounds, and both loops are inert at negative `room`, which is what a 16-column `wstat` produces.
- **Ordering 40 → 33 → 80 → 16.** Sound. Each step reaches something the one before cannot (status text clipping, status title, recovery, quadrant title), the grow-back is asserted before the section enters #88's region, `wquad` is still an unclipped 29 at the 33 step so the 16 step is the first excursion below its geometry, and `start()` calls `cleanup` before every later session, so the wrecked 16-column state cannot leak into the sections that follow. I confirmed the boundaries the README now quotes with fresh sessions each time: 30 columns and 14 rows recover, 29 and 13 do not.
- **The sensors block.** The extension is fine and the race runs in the safe direction: at 20 columns the caption sits in screen columns 3-19, so tmux's own clip to 19 preserves it, and a repaint that had not happened yet would make the `unwanted` at 19 fail rather than pass. The `expect`/`unwanted` pair straddling 19/20 pins both sides of that guard, and the #88 caveat on the final grow-back is accurate — after the excursion `wquad` is stretched, so what returns is the caption and not the display.

## Coverage and limits

I built with `-DSST_WERROR=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` (clean) and ran `tests/tui.sh <build>/sst Debug` on this exact worktree: `tui OK`. I did not run the compiled `ctest` suite, the golden recordings, or a Release build — that is the `verifier`'s round, which is owed anyway. I did not re-run your mutants; the guard behaviour I checked directly on screen instead. `draw_quad_line`'s clip marker remains uncovered, correctly deferred to #88.

## Verdict: **pass**, with two missing-coverage findings

No failing check, no flake, no regression against the merge-base. Everything the brief asked me to check hardest held up, except that one of the four new guards has no test at all.

---

## 1. Failures

None. Every check listed under "What ran" was green, on repeated runs.

---

## 2. Missing coverage

### 2a. The bare `" Quadrant "` guard has no test in either direction (new code, zero coverage)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:513-514`

```c
if (panel_room(wquad) >= (int)strlen(" Quadrant "))
	mvwaddstr(wquad, 0, 2, " Quadrant ");
```

Two mutants of this line pass the **entire** suite (all 11 ctest tests, Debug):

- `if (1)` — guard defeated
- `panel_room(wquad) > strlen(" Quadrant ")` — one column too strict

The guard is real. Driven by hand at 10 columns, clean build vs. the `if (1)` mutant:

```
clean                       mutant
lqqqqqqqqk                  lq Quadran
x     1 >x                  t     1 >x     <- the title wrapped onto the left border
```

That is the exact fault the diff exists to remove, and nothing catches it. The cause is width: `tests/tui.sh`'s narrowest resize is 16 columns, where `panel_room(wquad)` is 13 and the guard (threshold 10) is satisfied either way. The guard only engages below 13 columns.

This is the one guard of the four that `code-review`'s permissive-side fix did not reach — and unlike the others it is unpinned on *both* sides.

### 2b. The in-game title guard's permissive side is unpinned

`tui.c:527` — `panel_room(wquad) >= (int)strlen(" Quadrant 8 - 8 ")`

The mutant `>` instead of `>=` (coordinates dropped at 19 columns instead of 18) **survives the whole suite**. Its strict side is covered (`if (1)` fails at 16 columns), but nothing asserts the coordinates are still shown at 19 — the same asymmetry that was fixed for the caption. The sensors block does sit at 20 and 19 columns with a game running, so an assertion there would be nearly free.

For contrast, the `" Status "` guard *is* pinned on both sides: `>` instead of `>=` fails the 40-column precondition (`sub-minimum: the panels are not on screen to be checked`), exactly as the test's comment claims.

### 2c. Correction to a claim in the brief — `draw_quad_line`'s clip *is* covered

The brief and the note on #88 say it has none because it only engages below 29 columns. It does have coverage, incidentally: forcing `room = 1000` in `draw_quad_line` fails twice —

```
FAIL: sub-minimum: the quadrant title wrapped over the panel border
FAIL: sensors: the caption went early, before the room ran out
```

The 16-column dump shows the grid, not the title, spilling over the left border:

```
| lq Quadrant qqqk
| x     1 2 3 4 5
| 6  1  . . . . .      <- grid row wrapped onto column 1
```

Not a defect — but the failure message names the title for a break in the grid lines, which would send a maintainer to the wrong guard. Worth a word in the message or the comment; the #88 note understates what exists.

---

## 3. What I checked hardest, and what I found

### Item 1 — every new assertion, lexed rather than read

The `/></` → `/>/` fix is real, verified by lexing rather than by eye:

```
$ printf 'abc>def\nabc><def\n' | awk 'NR>=1 && /></ { print "OLD:", $0 }'
OLD: abc><def          <- old form matched only lines containing "><"
$ printf 'abc>def\nabc><def\n' | awk 'NR>=1 && />/ { print "NEW:", $0 }'
NEW: abc>def
NEW: abc><def
```

No `/></` remains in the file. Every new awk expression checked by lexing and by execution under mawk, busybox awk and nawk (macOS's awk itself is not available here — see environment gaps):

| expression | lexes as | can fire? |
|---|---|---|
| `uniform_col`'s body | `substr($0,col,1)` compared across rows; `exit (n>0 && !bad)?0:1` | yes — verified same/diff/empty input on three awks, and by mutants M3/M4/M7/M9 |
| `NR == 13 && /[0-9]/` | `$0 ~ /[0-9]/` | yes — fires on M7 |
| `substr($0, 39, 1) == ">"` (string, not regex) | pattern with default print, piped to `wc -l` | yes — fires on M1 |
| `NR >= 2 && NR <= 12 && />/` | `$0 ~ />/` | yes — fires on M8 |

The `elif` chaining was checked structurally: the three inner checks at 40 columns are independent `if`s; the two remaining `elif` chains are precondition→check, which is the correct use. `shellcheck -s sh tests/tui.sh` is clean.

I also probed a blindness the brief did not list: the three `SENSORS DAMAGED` **presence** assertions could have been satisfied by message-window text at 80 columns rather than by the caption. A mutant that never draws the caption (`if (0)`) fails all three, so none is blind:

```
FAIL: sensors: the grid gives no reason for its dashes
FAIL: sensors: the caption went early, before the room ran out
FAIL: sensors: the caption did not come back with the room for it
```

Staleness cannot produce a spurious pass anywhere in the new material: tmux truncates rather than reflows on shrink, so an unrepainted screen fails these checks rather than passing them.

### Item 2 — all mutants re-run by me, each against its own copy

Every mutant is a fresh `cp -a` of the current working tree outside the repository (stale `build-rel`/`build-warn`/`build-werror` directories that were sitting in the tree were removed from each copy), configured fresh. I printed `CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` from every cache and confirmed each points at its own copy, never at the repository. Control run of the unmutated copy: 0 failures.

### Item 3 — the three `tui.c` comment corrections, checked against the running game

**`panel_room()` returns `W-3`, text at columns 2..`getmaxx-2`.** Confirmed. At 13 columns the quadrant row reads `x     1 2 3>x`: border at 0-based col 0, text at cols 2..11 (10 = 13-3), right border at col 12 = `getmaxx-1`, so the last text column is `getmaxx-2`. The arithmetic sentence now matches the code.

**The 13-18 column in-game band shows the bare title.** Confirmed by a live sweep at every boundary the comment names:

```

 13 cols | row1=[lq Quadrant k]           <- bare title appears
 18 cols | row1=[lq Quadrant qqqqqk]      <- still bare, in a running game
```

All three thresholds in the comment (`" Status "` below 40, in-game title below 19, bare `" Quadrant "` below 13) are exactly right, and the caption's below-20 threshold is pinned by the test on both sides.

**The single-digit note.** `" Quadrant 8 - 8 "` is the width drawn, not an upper bound — consistent with everything observed.

Two further comment claims verified while I was there: `Shields       DAMAGED, 100% 2500.0 units` is exactly 40 characters and fits the 72-column status panel with nothing to spare and **no false marker** (`clip_at` correctly declines to mark an exact fit) — the #89 case; and the caption at 19 columns without its guard eats the bottom-right corner rather than wrapping, exactly as described (`mq SENSORS DAMAGED` with the `j` gone).

### Item 4 — builds, suites, plain mode, A/B

- **Builds:** Debug and Release, each with and without `-DSST_WERROR=ON`. All four configure and build; **zero warnings** in the non-`-Werror` builds.
- **Suites:** `ctest` on both build types, 11/11 passed each (184s / 178s).
- **Plain mode:** byte-identical to the merge-base on a deterministic seed (`tournament 7 short novice`, then srscan/lrscan/status/chart/damages/move/srscan/quit). - **README thresholds**, measured independently rather than taken from your note. Full-screen diff of the recovered panels against a never-shrunk session:
  - 30x24 → back to 80x24: **identical** (recovers)
  - 29x24 → back to 80x24: quadrant box's right border and top-right corner **gone** (does not recover)
  - 80x14 → back to 80x24: identical but for prompt position (recovers)
  - 80x13 → back to 80x24: quadrant box's **bottom border missing**, box stretched (does not recover)

  "under about thirty columns or fourteen rows" is correct as written.

### Journeys

Beyond `tests/tui.sh`: a tour of 40x24 → 16x24 → 5x24 → 72x3 → **1x1** → 20x24 → 80x24 in one running game. No crash, no hang, pane never died; `srscan` still accepted afterwards and Ctrl-D exited with status **0** and the farewell text. - **`cppcheck`, `clang-tidy` and `scan-build` are all absent.** No C static analysis ran beyond `-Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes -Werror`. Reporting this as a gap, not a pass.
