content.text:
## Verdict: **pass**, with two missing-coverage findings

No failing check, no flake, no regression against the merge-base. Everything the brief asked me to check hardest held up, except that one of the four new guards has no test at all.

---

## 1. Failures

None. Every check listed under "What ran" was green, on repeated runs.

---

## 2. Missing coverage

### 2a. The bare `" Quadrant "` guard has no test in either direction (new code, zero coverage)

`/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c:513-514`

```c
if (panel_room(wquad) >= (int)strlen(" Quadrant "))
	mvwaddstr(wquad, 0, 2, " Quadrant ");
```

Two mutants of this line pass the **entire** suite (all 11 ctest tests, Debug):

- `if (1)` — guard defeated
- `panel_room(wquad) > strlen(" Quadrant ")` — one column too strict

The guard is real. Driven by hand at 10 columns, clean build vs. the `if (1)` mutant:

```
clean                       mutant
lqqqqqqqqk                  lq Quadran
x     1 >x                  t     1 >x     <- the title wrapped onto the left border
```

That is the exact fault the diff exists to remove, and nothing catches it. The cause is width: `tests/tui.sh`'s narrowest resize is 16 columns, where `panel_room(wquad)` is 13 and the guard (threshold 10) is satisfied either way. The guard only engages below 13 columns.

This is the one guard of the four that `code-review`'s permissive-side fix did not reach — and unlike the others it is unpinned on *both* sides.

### 2b. The in-game title guard's permissive side is unpinned

`tui.c:527` — `panel_room(wquad) >= (int)strlen(" Quadrant 8 - 8 ")`

The mutant `>` instead of `>=` (coordinates dropped at 19 columns instead of 18) **survives the whole suite**. Its strict side is covered (`if (1)` fails at 16 columns), but nothing asserts the coordinates are still shown at 19 — the same asymmetry that was fixed for the caption. The sensors block does sit at 20 and 19 columns with a game running, so an assertion there would be nearly free.

For contrast, the `" Status "` guard *is* pinned on both sides: `>` instead of `>=` fails the 40-column precondition (`sub-minimum: the panels are not on screen to be checked`), exactly as the test's comment claims.

### 2c. Correction to a claim in the brief — `draw_quad_line`'s clip *is* covered

The brief and the note on #88 say it has none because it only engages below 29 columns. It does have coverage, incidentally: forcing `room = 1000` in `draw_quad_line` fails twice —

```
FAIL: sub-minimum: the quadrant title wrapped over the panel border
FAIL: sensors: the caption went early, before the room ran out
```

The 16-column dump shows the grid, not the title, spilling over the left border:

```
| lq Quadrant qqqk
| x     1 2 3 4 5
| 6  1  . . . . .      <- grid row wrapped onto column 1
```

Not a defect — but the failure message names the title for a break in the grid lines, which would send a maintainer to the wrong guard. Worth a word in the message or the comment; the #88 note understates what exists.

---

## 3. What I checked hardest, and what I found

### Item 1 — every new assertion, lexed rather than read

The `/></` → `/>/` fix is real, verified by lexing rather than by eye:

```
$ printf 'abc>def\nabc><def\n' | awk 'NR>=1 && /></ { print "OLD:", $0 }'
OLD: abc><def          <- old form matched only lines containing "><"
$ printf 'abc>def\nabc><def\n' | awk 'NR>=1 && />/ { print "NEW:", $0 }'
NEW: abc>def
NEW: abc><def
```

No `/></` remains in the file. Every new awk expression checked by lexing and by execution under mawk, busybox awk and nawk (macOS's awk itself is not available here — see environment gaps):

| expression | lexes as | can fire? |
|---|---|---|
| `uniform_col`'s body | `substr($0,col,1)` compared across rows; `exit (n>0 && !bad)?0:1` | yes — verified same/diff/empty input on three awks, and by mutants M3/M4/M7/M9 |
| `NR == 13 && /[0-9]/` | `$0 ~ /[0-9]/` | yes — fires on M7 |
| `substr($0, 39, 1) == ">"` (string, not regex) | pattern with default print, piped to `wc -l` | yes — fires on M1 |
| `NR >= 2 && NR <= 12 && />/` | `$0 ~ />/` | yes — fires on M8 |

The `elif` chaining was checked structurally: the three inner checks at 40 columns are independent `if`s; the two remaining `elif` chains are precondition→check, which is the correct use. `shellcheck -s sh tests/tui.sh` is clean.

I also probed a blindness the brief did not list: the three `SENSORS DAMAGED` **presence** assertions could have been satisfied by message-window text at 80 columns rather than by the caption. A mutant that never draws the caption (`if (0)`) fails all three, so none is blind:

```
FAIL: sensors: the grid gives no reason for its dashes
FAIL: sensors: the caption went early, before the room ran out
FAIL: sensors: the caption did not come back with the room for it
```

Staleness cannot produce a spurious pass anywhere in the new material: tmux truncates rather than reflows on shrink, so an unrepainted screen fails these checks rather than passing them.

### Item 2 — all mutants re-run by me, each against its own copy

Every mutant is a fresh `cp -a` of the current working tree outside the repository (stale `build-rel`/`build-warn`/`build-werror` directories that were sitting in the tree were removed from each copy), configured fresh. I printed `CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` from every cache and confirmed each points at its own copy, never at the repository. Control run of the unmutated copy: 0 failures.

| # | mutant | result | caught by |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | clip marker removed (`clip_at` returns `s[i]`) | **caught** | `a clipped status line does not say it was clipped` |
| M2 | bare `" Quadrant "` guard → `if (1)` | **SURVIVES** | — (finding 2a) |
| M3 | `" Status "` guard → `if (1)` | **caught** | `the status title wrapped over the panel border` |
| M4 | in-game title guard → `if (1)` | **caught** | `the quadrant title wrapped over the panel border` |
| M5 | caption guard → `if (sensors_masked())` | **caught** | `the caption overran the box it captions` |
| M6 | caption guard one column too strict | **caught** | `the caption went early, before the room ran out` |
| M7 | `draw_status_line`'s `room` forced to 1000 | **caught** (4 assertions) | border, bottom border, marker, status title |
| M8 | widening step removed from the test | **caught** (2 assertions) | `widening did not bring the clipped lines back`, `a clip marker survived the widening` |
| M9 | `draw_quad_line`'s `room` forced to 1000 | **caught** | see 2c |
| M10 | caption never drawn (`if (0)`) | **caught** (3 assertions) | see item 1 |
| M11 | `" Status "` guard one column too strict | **caught** | `the panels are not on screen to be checked` |
| M12 | in-game title guard one column too strict | **SURVIVES** | — (finding 2b) |
| M13 | bare `" Quadrant "` guard one column too strict | **SURVIVES** | — (finding 2a) |

Every claim in your table reproduced. M2/M12/M13 are mine.

### Item 3 — the three `tui.c` comment corrections, checked against the running game

**`panel_room()` returns `W-3`, text at columns 2..`getmaxx-2`.** Confirmed. At 13 columns the quadrant row reads `x     1 2 3>x`: border at 0-based col 0, text at cols 2..11 (10 = 13-3), right border at col 12 = `getmaxx-1`, so the last text column is `getmaxx-2`. The arithmetic sentence now matches the code.

**The 13-18 column in-game band shows the bare title.** Confirmed by a live sweep at every boundary the comment names:

```
 12 cols | row1=[lqqqqqqqqqqk]            <- no title
 13 cols | row1=[lq Quadrant k]           <- bare title appears
 18 cols | row1=[lq Quadrant qqqqqk]      <- still bare, in a running game
 19 cols | row1=[lq Quadrant 3 - 2 k]     <- coordinates appear
 39 cols | row1=[... lqqqqqqqqk]          <- no " Status "
 40 cols | row1=[... lq Status k]         <- " Status " appears
```

All three thresholds in the comment (`" Status "` below 40, in-game title below 19, bare `" Quadrant "` below 13) are exactly right, and the caption's below-20 threshold is pinned by the test on both sides.

**The single-digit note.** `" Quadrant 8 - 8 "` is the width drawn, not an upper bound — consistent with everything observed.

Two further comment claims verified while I was there: `Shields       DAMAGED, 100% 2500.0 units` is exactly 40 characters and fits the 72-column status panel with nothing to spare and **no false marker** (`clip_at` correctly declines to mark an exact fit) — the #89 case; and the caption at 19 columns without its guard eats the bottom-right corner rather than wrapping, exactly as described (`mq SENSORS DAMAGED` with the `j` gone).

### Item 4 — builds, suites, plain mode, A/B

- **Builds:** Debug and Release, each with and without `-DSST_WERROR=ON`. All four configure and build; **zero warnings** in the non-`-Werror` builds.
- **Suites:** `ctest` on both build types, 11/11 passed each (184s / 178s).
- **Plain mode:** byte-identical to the merge-base on a deterministic seed (`tournament 7 short novice`, then srscan/lrscan/status/chart/damages/move/srscan/quit). The unseeded `regular` journey differs, which I confirmed is the game's own randomness — the merge-base binary differs from itself on the same input.
- **TUI A/B at 72x24 and 80x24** against a merge-base build, with S.R. Sensors *and* Shields damaged via `debug`: panel rows 1-13 **identical** at both sizes.
- **README thresholds**, measured independently rather than taken from your note. Full-screen diff of the recovered panels against a never-shrunk session:
  - 30x24 → back to 80x24: **identical** (recovers)
  - 29x24 → back to 80x24: quadrant box's right border and top-right corner **gone** (does not recover)
  - 80x14 → back to 80x24: identical but for prompt position (recovers)
  - 80x13 → back to 80x24: quadrant box's **bottom border missing**, box stretched (does not recover)

  "under about thirty columns or fourteen rows" is correct as written.

### Journeys

Beyond `tests/tui.sh`: a tour of 40x24 → 16x24 → 5x24 → 72x3 → **1x1** → 20x24 → 80x24 in one running game. No crash, no hang, pane never died; `srscan` still accepted afterwards and Ctrl-D exited with status **0** and the farewell text. The permanent distortion after going below the panels' geometry is #88, as filed.

---

## 4. Environment issues

- **`cppcheck`, `clang-tidy` and `scan-build` are all absent.** No C static analysis ran beyond `-Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes -Werror`. Reporting this as a gap, not a pass.
- **macOS's `awk` (BWK "one true awk") is not installed here.** The new awk expressions were exercised under mawk, busybox awk and nawk (a mawk symlink on this box) — three implementations, but not the one the comment specifically names for CI's macOS leg. The constructs used (`-v` numeric coercion, uninitialized scalars, `exit <ternary>`, bare-ERE patterns) are all POSIX, so the risk is low, but it is untested on the target.
- Stale `build-rel/`, `build-warn/`, `build-werror/` directories are sitting in the working tree (gitignored, so invisible to `git status`). They were removed from every mutant copy to avoid the cache-path trap; they do not affect the verdict.

---

## 5. What ran (for reproduction)

Scope: the working-tree diff against merge-base `966ccf1` — `README.md`, `tests/tui.sh`, `tui.c`. No commits on the branch; all three files are unstaged modifications. No untracked files. `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `tui.c`, `tests/tui.sh` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` were all read from disk.

```sh
# builds (4)
cmake -S . -B build-debug   -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug   -DSST_WERROR=ON && cmake --build build-debug -j
cmake -S . -B build-release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSST_WERROR=ON && cmake --build build-release -j
# plus both types without SST_WERROR, warning count checked

# suites
ctest --test-dir build-debug   --output-on-failure     # 11/11
ctest --test-dir build-release --output-on-failure     # 11/11

# flake probe: 3 sequential + 4 concurrent under 24-way CPU load
./tests/tui.sh ./build-debug/sst Debug                 # 7 extra runs, 0 failures

# mutants: 13, each a fresh copy outside the repo with its own cmake cache
<copy>/tests/tui.sh <copy>/build/sst Debug
ctest --test-dir <copy>/build                          # for M2

# static
shellcheck -s sh tests/tui.sh                          # clean
```

tmux ran on private sockets only (`verif`…`verif8-$PID`, `-f /dev/null -L`), plus `tests/tui.sh`'s own `sst-tui-$$`. Every server I started is dead and its socket file removed; no other socket in `/tmp/tmux-1000/` was touched, and no bare `kill-server` was issued. The repository is unmodified — `git status` still shows exactly the three files it showed at the start.
Verifier passed it but found the bare `" Quadrant "` guard has no test at all — its threshold is 13 columns and my narrowest check was 16. Closing that and the permissive side of the in-game title:

cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
gh issue create --title "A terminal too short runs the panel rows together, the way a narrow one used to run its columns" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

#78 stopped panel *lines* from wrapping over their own borders when the
terminal is too narrow. The same fault exists on the other axis and is
untouched: shrink a full-screen game below 13 rows and the grid rows
collide with each other and with the bottom border.

At 72x11, on a build with #78's fix:

```
x  8  . . . . . . . . . *   xx Shields       DOWN, 100% 2500.0 units   x
mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .x Klingons Left 2                         x
```

Two grid rows merged onto the bottom border — the same shape as the
`     7.00qj` that #78 reported, rotated ninety degrees. Clean at 13
rows, garbled at 12 and below.

## Why

`draw_quad_line()` and `draw_status_line()` start with `wmove(w, row, 2)`.
When `resize_term()` has shrunk the window below `PANELH`, that row no
longer exists: `wmove` returns ERR and leaves the cursor where it was, so
the `waddch` loop that follows writes onto whatever row the cursor was
already on. #78 bounded the loops by *column* — `panel_room()` — and
nothing checks the row.

The obvious fix is symmetric: skip the line when `row >= getmaxy(w)`, or
check `wmove`'s return before drawing. `tui_refresh_panels()` draws rows
1-11 unconditionally, so the check belongs in the two draw functions or
in the loops that call them.

## Scope

Pre-existing and identical on the merge-base — #78 neither causes nor
addresses it, and its README paragraph is now worded to claim clipping
for narrowing only, with a sentence pointing at this behavior for short
terminals.

Distinct from #88, which is about the display not coming *back* after a
shrink. This is what is on screen while you are down there, and it is
visible at 11 rows without ever leaving the size.

## How to see it

```sh
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch new-session -d -x 100 -y 30 -s t './build/sst -t'
# answer the setup questions, get to COMMAND>
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch resize-window -t t -x 72 -y 11
tmux -f /dev/null -L scratch capture-pane -t t -p
```

Your own socket (`-L`) as above, never the default one, and never a bare
`tmux kill-server`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No panel line is drawn onto another line's row at any height.
- [ ] Covered in `tests/tui.sh`, which now sweeps widths in its
      sub-minimum section and could sweep heights the same way.

Found by `code-review` on the branch for #78. Follow the workflow in
[AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
)"
tests/tui.sh ./build/sst Debug 2>&1 | grep -E '^(FAIL|tui )'

fix(tui): clip the panels instead of wrapping them

A terminal dragged below the 72x24 the display asks for garbled the
panels: `xorWarp Fact`, `xLeTime Left`, a bottom border reading
`     7.00qj`.

#78 diagnosed this as the two panels overlapping. They do not, and the
issue is corrected by comment. The leading `x` in `xorWarp Fact` is the
quadrant panel's own right border, in its correct column; what follows
is the status panel writing over its own. draw_status_line() walked its
string with waddch and nothing stopped it at the window edge, and waddch
past the last column wraps to the next row of the same window -- so the
tail of a line too long to fit landed on the row below, on that row's
left border and padding, and for the last line on the bottom border.
`ts`, in `xtsKlingons Left 2` at 66 columns, is the end of `units`.

panel_room() bounds both draw loops. That alone would clip in silence,
which ui-review found is worse than the wrapping: what is left reads as
a smaller and perfectly plausible reading of the same field -- three
torpedoes' worth of `Torpedoes     1` for ten of them, `Energy 367` for
3675.25 -- on a panel that now looks intact and so gets believed.
Garbage announced itself; a truncated number does not. So clip_at()
spends a clipped line's last column on a `>`.

Four strings in the panels are written whole rather than a cell at a
time and needed room asked for separately: both titles, the in-game one
that replaces the first, and the SENSORS DAMAGED caption -- which
review found after the first three, having been missed by the comment
that claimed the titles were the only ones. Each is now drawn only when
it fits: below 40, 19, 13 and 20 columns respectively they are dropped.
Dropped rather than shortened, on ui-review's judgment: the dashes
still tell a player their sensors are out, and every abbreviation
invents a misreading rather than removing one.

Two claims of mine in comments were wrong and are corrected. The
quadrant window is not a fixed 29 columns -- resize_term() shrinks every
window that no longer fits, so its title wraps too. And the longest
status line is not 37 columns but 40, `Shields       DAMAGED, 100%
2500.0 units`, against exactly 40 columns of room at the 72-column
minimum: an exact fit with nothing to spare, which nothing checks. That
is filed as #89.

Nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24. Verified byte-identical to the
merge-base over a full journey at both sizes, with sensors and shields
damaged.

tests/tui.sh gains a width sweep -- 40, 33, back to 80, then 19, 18, 16,
13, 12 -- and two widths in the sensors block. Every assertion was
proven able to fail by building a mutant in a copy outside the
repository, with CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY checked so the break reached the
binary: the marker removed, each of the four guards defeated, each
guard made one column too strict, and the bound removed entirely, which
fails four assertions at once. Two of my own assertions could not fail
when written and were caught by review -- one awk regex written `/></`,
which lexes as `><` and never matched, and one chained behind a check
that hid it.

Filed, not fixed: #88 (shrinking under the panels' geometry and back
leaves the display broken), #89 above, #90 (the columns outside every
window keep text from a wider terminal), #91 (a terminal too short runs
the panel rows together -- the same fault on the other axis, which this
fix does not touch, and which the README now warns about).

Passes: ui-review three rounds, verifier three, code-review three. The
second ui-review round found the silent-clipping defect above and the
third judged the dropped caption; the verifier failed the branch once,
on a README threshold that was still off by one; code-review found the
missed caption, the unfireable assertion, and an overclaim in the
README that promised clipping on an axis this fix does not bound.

Closes #78

Closes #78.

## The premise was wrong, and correcting it changed the fix

#78 diagnosed the garbling below 72x24 as the two panels overlapping.
**They do not overlap.** In `xorWarp Fact` the leading `x` is the
quadrant panel's own right border, intact and in its correct column;
what follows is the status panel writing over **its own**.

`draw_status_line()` walked its string with `waddch` and nothing stopped
it at the window edge — and `waddch` past the last column wraps to the
next row of the *same* window. So the tail of a line too long to fit
landed on the row below, over that row's left border and padding, and
for the last line over the bottom border. Clearest at 66 columns, where
exactly two characters overrun:

```
x  8  . . . . . . E . . .   xx Shields       DOWN, 100% 2500.0 uni
x  9  . . . . . . . . . .   xtsKlingons Left 2                   x
```

`ts` is the end of `units`.

The issue offered two options as a design choice. With the cause
understood, option 2 is not a choice but the bug fix, and it makes the
comment at `tui.c` true as written. Posted as a
[comment on #78](../issues/78) rather than editing the body. I also
confirmed the two claims the issue got right: the garbling predates #79
and reproduces on `dbcaa63`, and #79 changed only how often a player
sees it — verified by `SIGSTOP`ping the game before the drag, which
proves the fragments are the game's own drawing and not a tmux artifact.

## The fix

`panel_room()` bounds both draw loops. That alone clips in *silence*,
which `ui-review` found is worse than the wrapping it replaces: what is
left reads as a smaller, perfectly plausible value — `Torpedoes     1`
for ten of them, `Energy        367` for 3675.25 — on a panel that now
looks intact and so gets believed. Garbage announces itself; a truncated
number does not. So `clip_at()` spends a clipped line's last column on
a `>`.

Four strings are written whole rather than a cell at a time and needed
room asked for separately — both titles, the in-game one that replaces
the first, and the `SENSORS DAMAGED` caption. The caption was found by
`code-review` *after* the first three, having been missed by the comment
claiming the titles were the only ones. Each is now drawn only when it
fits, and dropped rather than shortened on `ui-review`'s judgment: the
dashes still tell a player their sensors are out, and every abbreviation
invents a misreading rather than removing one.

**Nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24** — verified byte-identical to the
merge-base over a full journey at both sizes, with sensors and shields
damaged.

## Two comments of mine were wrong

- The quadrant window is **not** a fixed 29 columns. `resize_term()`
  shrinks every window that no longer fits, so its title wraps too.
- The longest status line is **40** columns, not 37:
  `Shields       DAMAGED, 100% 2500.0 units`, against exactly 40 columns
  of room at the minimum. An exact fit with nothing to spare, which
  nothing checks — filed as #89.

## Tests

A width sweep — 40, 33, back to 80, then 19, 18, 16, 13, 12 — plus two
widths in the sensors block. Every assertion was proven able to fail by
building a mutant in a copy **outside** the repository with
`CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` checked, so the break reached the binary: the
marker removed, each of the four guards defeated, each guard made one
column too strict, and the bound removed entirely (which fails four
assertions at once).

Two assertions of mine could not fire when written, both caught by
review: one awk regex written `/></`, which lexes as the regex `><` and
never matched anything the panels draw, and one chained as the `elif` of
a check that hid it. Both were in code written *in response to* findings
about assertions that cannot fail.

## Issues filed

- **#88** — shrinking under the panels' geometry and back leaves the
  display broken, at ordinary widths afterwards
- **#89** — nothing pins that status lines fit at 72 columns
- **#90** — the columns outside every window keep text from a wider
  terminal
- **#91** — a terminal too *short* runs the panel rows together: the
  same fault on the other axis, which this fix does not bound

second `ui-review` round found the silent-clipping defect; the third
judged the dropped caption. The `verifier` failed the branch once, on a
README threshold still off by one — the display needs `PANELH + 1` rows,
which I confirmed myself before believing it. `code-review` found the
missed caption, the unfireable assertion, and a README claim that
promised clipping on an axis this fix does not bound.

both. Plain mode byte-identical on deterministic seeds.

content.text:
PR #92 is open and CI is running — the one thing I can't check locally is macOS's `awk`, which is why the non-POSIX `length(array)` idiom got replaced. I'll squash-merge once it's green.

**#78, and what it actually was.** The issue's diagnosis was wrong in a way that changed the fix: nothing overlapped. `draw_status_line()` had no bound, and `waddch` past the last column wraps to the next row of the *same* window — so a too-long status line landed on the row below, over its border and padding, and for the last line over the bottom border. At 66 columns you can watch exactly two characters do it: `ts`, the end of `units`, appearing as `xtsKlingons Left 2`.

Three things I'd flag, all found by reviewers rather than by me:

- **Silent clipping was worse than the bug.** My first cut just bounded the loop, which turned `Torpedoes     10` into `Torpedoes     1` — a plausible wrong number on a panel that now looks intact. Garbage announces itself; that doesn't. Hence the `>` marker.
- **Two comments I wrote were false.** `resize_term()` does shrink the quadrant window, and the longest status line is 40 columns, not 37 — an exact fit against the room available at 72, with nothing to spare.
- **Two of my assertions couldn't fire**, both in code I wrote *responding to* findings about assertions that can't fire. One was `/></`, which awk lexes as the regex `><`. Everything now has a mutant behind it, built outside the repo with the cache path checked.

**Filed:** #88, #89, #90, #91. #91 is the one worth your attention — a terminal too *short* runs the panel rows together, the same fault on the other axis, which this fix does not bound. The README says so for now, and #91 carries a criterion to remove that sentence when it's fixed.

## What happened

The commit for #78 (`c2fd28b`) contains, on one line:

```
Filed, not fixed: #88 (shrinking under the panels' geometry and back
```

GitHub matched the substring `fixed: #88`, treated it as a closing
keyword, and closed #88 on merge — an issue the same sentence says is
*not* fixed, and which that change reproduced on its own merge-base. It
was reopened by hand.

## Why it will happen again

AGENTS.md step 9 asks every change to say which issues were filed, "in
the pull request body and in the summary of the work". Those lists sit
next to phrases like "filed, not fixed", "fixed in #x, not here", and
"this does not fix #y" — every one of which contains a closing keyword
followed by a reference. The workflow that requires the disclosure is
what creates the hazard, so it is worth handling rather than
remembering.

GitHub's keywords are `close`/`closes`/`closed`, `fix`/`fixes`/`fixed`,
`resolve`/`resolves`/`resolved`, each matched with an optional colon
before the reference and **without regard to the words in front of it**.

## Suggested approach

Cheapest is a wording convention plus something that checks it:

- Refer to issues that a change does *not* fix without a keyword
  anywhere before the number — "left open: #88", "see #88", "filed as
  #88". Reserve `Closes #n` for the issue the change actually closes,
  on a line of its own.
- Have the tests check it. `tests/instructions.sh` already reads files
  and asserts things about them; a check over `git log` on the branch
  for a keyword-plus-reference that is not on its own line would catch
  this before merge. That is where the "prove it can fail" work goes:
  break it by writing "not fixed: #1" in a scratch commit.

Worth also fixing the wording in `AGENTS.md` step 9 itself if it ends up
recommending a phrasing, so the guidance and the check agree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A commit or PR body can name an unfixed issue without closing it.
- [ ] Something automated catches the mistake, and is proven able to
      fail.

Found while merging #92; #88 was the casualty. Follow the workflow in
[AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).
EOF
)"

content.text:
Merged as `c2fd28b`, all four CI legs green, #78 closed.

**One thing to know about:** the merge closed **#88 by accident**. My commit body said `Filed, not fixed: #88 (...)` and GitHub matched the substring `fixed: #88` as a closing keyword — closing the very issue the sentence says isn't fixed. I've reopened it with a comment explaining why, and verified #89/#90/#91 were unaffected.

That's a trap the workflow walks into by design: AGENTS.md step 9 requires every change to list the issues it filed, and those lists naturally contain phrases like "filed, not fixed" and "this does not fix #y" — each one a closing keyword followed by a reference. Filed as **#93**, with a suggested convention (no keyword before a number you aren't closing) and a check to enforce it.

**#78 itself.** The issue's diagnosis was wrong and correcting it changed the fix: nothing overlapped, `draw_status_line()` simply had no bound, and `waddch` past the last column wraps onto the next row of the same window. The three things worth your attention, all found by reviewers rather than by me:

- **Bounding the loop silently was worse than the bug** — `Torpedoes     10` became `Torpedoes     1` on a panel that now looked trustworthy. Hence the `>` marker.
- **Two of my comments asserted things that were false** — that `resize_term()` leaves the quadrant window alone, and that the longest status line is 37 columns. It's 40, an exact fit against the room at 72 with nothing to spare (#89).
- **Two of my assertions couldn't fire**, both written in response to findings about assertions that can't fire. One was `/></`, which awk lexes as the regex `><`.

Open now: #91 (the same fault on the vertical axis, which this fix doesn't bound), #90, #89, #88, #93, plus the agent-definition items #86/#85/#84/#81 and #76/#65.

content.text: Confirmed, and it's two distinct modes: at 12 rows `draw_quad_line(11)` writes *onto* the border row (in bounds, wrong row); at 11 `wmove` fails outright and the lines pile up. Test first:

input.command:
cd /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek
python3 - <<'PY'
p='tests/tui.sh'; t=open(p).read()
anchor = "# --- Ctrl-D ends the session on its own keystroke ---------------------"
new = """# --- a shrink past the panels' height clips too ------------------------
# The width sweep above is only half of it. The panels are PANELH rows
# deep, and a terminal shorter than that shrinks them with it -- but the
# draw loops were told which row to write on by the caller and never
# asked whether that row still existed. Two ways to fail, one on each
# side of the last row: at twelve rows the tenth grid line was drawn
# onto the bottom border, and at eleven wmove() failed outright, left
# the cursor where it was, and the line landed on the row above --
# `mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .x`, two grid rows and the border in one.
#
# Twelve and eleven because they are those two cases; nine for a shrink
# well past both.
start 100 30 'tournament 7 short novice pw'
if ! to_command; then
	fail "short: the game never reached its command prompt"
	dump
else
	for h in 12 11 9; do
		tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 72 -y "$h"
		sleep 1
		# The panels fill a screen this short, so the last row of it
		# is their bottom border. Nothing numeric belongs there --
		# the only caption it ever carries is SENSORS DAMAGED -- and
		# a grid line that landed on it brings its row label along.
		if ! screen | head -1 | grep -qF 'Quadrant'; then
			fail "short: the panels are not on screen at 72x$h"
			dump
		elif ! screen | awk -v h="$h" 'NR == h && /[0-9]/ { bad = 1 }
		                               END { exit bad ? 1 : 0 }'; then
			fail "short: a panel line was drawn onto the bottom border at 72x$h"
			dump
		fi
	done
	# And the rows that do fit are still one per line: a line that
	# landed on the row above leaves two labels on it.
	tm resize-window -t "$session" -x 72 -y 11
	sleep 1
	if [ "$(screen | grep -c '^x  *[0-9][0-9]*  ')" -ne "$(screen | grep -c '^x  *[0-9][0-9]*  ' | head -1)" ]; then
		:
	fi
	if screen | grep -qE '^.q? *[0-9]+ .*[0-9]+ +\\.'; then
		fail "short: two grid rows were drawn onto one line"
		dump
	fi
fi

"""
assert t.count(anchor)==1
open(p,'w').write(t.replace(anchor, new + anchor, 1)); print("section added")
PY
sh -n tests/tui.sh && echo "syntax ok"

Review the player-facing behavior of branch `fix/tui-short-terminal` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek. Closes #91. Read `AGENTS.md` and anything you check against from the repository, not from a copy in your context. `./build/sst` is current with the working tree; two files changed, `tui.c` and `tests/tui.sh`.

**The bug.** #78 bounded the panel draw loops by *column*. Nothing bounded them by *row*, and the caller always asks for all eleven lines however short the terminal is. Two failure modes on either side of the last row: at 12 rows the tenth grid line was drawn *onto* the bottom border (in bounds, wrong row); at 11 `wmove` failed outright, left the cursor where the previous line left it, and the whole line landed on the row above — `mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .x`, two grid rows and the border sharing one line.

**The fix.** `panel_has_row()` — the same question `panel_room()` asks on the other axis — and both draw loops return early when the row is not inside the box. Plus one thing that surprised me: `make_windows()` was resizing the status panel back to its full 13 rows on every repaint regardless of screen height, so it stayed taller than the screen, its bottom border fell off the bottom, and its last line was drawn where that border should have been. It now follows the screen the way the quadrant panel already did.

**What I want judged, as a games/CLI expert.**

1. **Rows now clip from the bottom, silently.** At 9 rows the grid shows rows 1-6 and the status panel shows Stardate through Energy; Klingons Left and Time Left are simply gone. #78 decided that clipping a *line* in silence was unacceptable and added a `>` marker, on the grounds that a truncated value reads as a smaller plausible value. Is a missing row the same problem or a different one? My reading is that it is different — the grid rows carry visible labels so a player can see the numbering stops at 6, and a missing status line is absent rather than wrong — but that is exactly the kind of call the `>` marker came from, so I want it from someone who did not write this. If you think the bottom border should carry a marker when rows were dropped, say so; it already carries `SENSORS DAMAGED` when sensors are out, so there is precedent and a conflict to think about.

2. **Which rows to drop.** It currently drops from the bottom, so the status panel loses Klingons Left and Time Left first — arguably two of the more important fields — while keeping Stardate and Condition. I did not consider reordering and I am not proposing it, but if you think the drop order actively misleads, that is worth knowing.

3. **What happens below 13 rows generally.** The message window lives at row `PANELH` and is off-screen entirely once the terminal is that short, so the player sees panels and no conversation and no `COMMAND>` prompt at all. That is pre-existing and not something this change touches, but I have not found it filed anywhere — if you confirm it, I will file it.

Also please check: nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24 (the claim the slice rests on); the boxes close properly at every height from 24 down to about 4; growing back afterwards. On growing back you will see the quadrant panel stay stretched with no bottom border while the status panel recovers — that is #88, pre-existing and unchanged by this fix, and the one-line place to fix it is now visibly adjacent to my change. Say if you think that makes leaving it wrong.

content.text:
## Verdict

**Acceptable as-is on the code, with one should-fix outside it: `README.md` still tells players the panels garble on a short terminal, which this change is exactly what stops being true.** The fix itself reads well at every height I could produce. Boxes close cleanly from 24 rows down to 1, rows clip from the bottom with no collisions, the row labels stay legible, `>` column clipping and the `SENSORS DAMAGED` caption still behave at their supported sizes, and 80x24 and 72x24 are byte-for-byte what `main` shows — the claim the slice rests on holds. I confirmed the two failure modes on a freshly built `main` (at 12 rows `mq10  . . . . . . . . . .qqqjx Time Left     7.00`, at 11 the `mq 9 ... .10 .x` collision the issue reports), and the status panel's last line landing on the border at both — so the `make_windows()` half of the fix is a real, separately visible defect, not a tidy-up. On your three questions: silent row clipping is the right call, the bottom-first drop order is the right call, and the missing message window below 14 rows is real, pre-existing and worth filing. The one thing I'd push back on inside `tui.c` is the `SENSORS DAMAGED` caption, which the fix leaves as the last surviving hardcoded row.

## Findings

**1. should-fix — `README.md:30-33` now documents the bug you fixed.**
Player experience: the only place a player is told what a resize does still says "Squeezed under about thirty columns or fourteen rows they break up instead — a terminal too short runs the panel rows together rather than clipping them". A player reading that will not shrink the window, and a player who does will find the documentation wrong in the game's favour, which is the kind of error that makes the rest of the paragraph less believable. Suggestion: fold the row axis into the clipping paragraph above it (`README.md:24-28`) — rows clip from the bottom the way columns clip from the right, the grid keeps its numbering so you can see where it stops — and keep a reduced version of the last sentence for what is *still* broken. Be careful with the recovery promise: line 28 says "Widening the terminal brings the panels straight back", and I verified that shrinking to **exactly 13 rows** and back to 80x24 already leaves the quadrant panel stretched over the message window with no prompt (#88). Whatever replaces lines 30-33 must not promise that height comes back.

**2. should-fix (or file) — `tui.c:565-566`, the `SENSORS DAMAGED` caption is the one row the fix does not reach.**
`mvwaddstr(wquad, PANELH-1, 2, " SENSORS DAMAGED ")` still names row 12 absolutely. ncurses' `mvwaddstr` checks `wmove`, so nothing is misdrawn — but from 12 rows down the caption is silently gone. I damaged the S.R. sensors through the `debug` command and watched it: at 72x13 the caption is on the border; at 72x12, 72x11 and 72x9 the player gets a full grid of `- - - -` with no reason given anywhere on screen. That is precisely what the comment above it says must not happen ("Without it the dashes are a field of nothing with no reason given"). It is pre-existing — on `main` the caption is equally absent at those heights, buried under the garbling — but it is the same question `panel_has_row()` was invented to ask, one line away, and after this change it is the only place in the panel that still assumes row 12 exists. Suggestion: draw it on the window's real last row (`getmaxy(wquad)-1`), with a floor so it does not land on the title row of a one- or two-row box. If you'd rather keep the slice thin, file it — but it should not go unmentioned, since it is the one player-visible short-terminal defect a reader would expect this change to have covered.

**3. No change — silent row clipping is correct, and I would not add a marker.** Two reasons beyond the ones you gave. First, the `>` marker answers an error of commission: `Energy        36>` exists because `Energy        367` is a *readable wrong number*. A dropped row leaves no wrong number; `Klingons Left` is absent along with its label, and nothing on the panel can be misread. Second, and decisive: rows only ever drop when the panel window is under 13 rows, and the message window sits at row `PANELH`, so **every height at which a row is dropped is a height with no conversation and no `COMMAND>` prompt at all** — I confirmed 72x13 and below show panels only. A "some rows are hidden" marker would be addressing a player who has already lost the prompt and is unmistakably in a too-small terminal; it tells them nothing they cannot see and offers no action they are not already taking. Adding one would also collide with `SENSORS DAMAGED` for the one border row available, and losing the damage notice to make room for "there is more below" would be a bad trade.

**4. No change — the drop order is right, and reordering would be worse.** `AGENTS.md` makes `srscan()` the spec that `tuifmt.c` must mirror exactly, and `fmt_status_line()`'s order is that order — Stardate through Time Left, as in the classic display. Prioritising Klingons Left and Time Left under truncation would mean the panel's field order changes as the player drags the window, which is a far worse read than two missing lines. Losing them at ≤12 rows costs nothing recoverable anyway, per finding 3: there is no `COMMAND>` to type `srscan` at down there.

**5. Confirmed for filing — below 14 rows there is no message window, no conversation and no prompt.** `wmsg` is created at row `PANELH` and `msgh` is clamped to 1, so at 13 rows and below the window is entirely off-screen. `main` behaves identically at 13 rows, so this change neither causes nor worsens it. Two details worth putting in the issue: the threshold is 14 rows, not 13 (at 72x14 the prompt is on the last line and the game reads normally); and it is only reachable by resizing mid-game, since startup still refuses and prints `Terminal too small (need 72x24) -- using classic display.` at 71x24 and at 72x12. I found nothing filed for it. It is arguably a facet of #88 but distinct: #88 is about not coming back, this is about there being no prompt while you are there.

**6. Judgment, not a blocker — leaving #88 is defensible, but say so where a player will read it.** I confirmed grow-back is identical on branch and `main` (fresh session, 100x30 → 72x9 → 80x24, no narrow steps: quadrant panel stretched, status panel recovered, message window and prompt gone). So the fix is neutral there and step 9 says not to fix it in this slice. The honest framing for the PR body is that the benefit is confined to the time spent short: any height where the new clipping is visible is a height that leaves the display unrecoverable on the way back. That is an argument for landing #88 next, not for widening this diff — but it *is* an argument against a README rewrite that reads as if short terminals are now fine. Handle it in finding 1's wording and I'm satisfied.

**7. Nit, pre-existing, width axis — a stray glyph and a one-column status panel below 30 columns.** At 28x24 the status panel is entirely off-screen and a leftover `5` sits at column 27 of the `COMMAND>` row, outside every window (residue on `stdscr` from the wider layout). At 30x8 the status panel renders as a one-column `k`/`x`/`j` sliver beside the quadrant box. Neither is touched by this change (both reproduce on `main`, both are the `statw`/`msgw` clamps from #78's era). Mentioning only so it is not mistaken for fallout — worth a line on #88 or a small issue of its own if not already covered.

## What I exercised

All TUI work on my own sockets (`-L uirev91`, `-L uirev91b`, `-f /dev/null`), sessions I created only, killed on those sockets at the end; the working tree is unchanged (`git status` still shows only your `tui.c` and `tests/tui.sh`).

- Read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md:5-40`, `sst.doc:1541-1550` (the full-screen paragraph — it says nothing about resizing, so no doc change is needed there), issues #91, #78, #88, and `tui.c` around `panel_room`/`panel_has_row`/`make_windows`/`tui_refresh_panels`.
- Built the branch (`cmake --build build`) and built `main` independently in `…/scratchpad/mainsrc` from `git archive main` with a fresh configure, per the copy-outside-the-tree rule, to compare.
- Full game journey to `COMMAND>` (`tournament 7 / short / novice / pw`, space through the banner) at 100x30, then the baseline captures at 80x24 and 72x24 — identical to `main`.
- Height sweep at 72 columns: 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, and then 3, 2, 1. Boxes close at every one; no collisions, no crash, no garbled sequences.
- Same sweep on the `main` binary at 13/12/11/9, reproducing both reported failure modes and the status panel's last line on the border.
- Combined narrow-and-short: 40x10, 30x8, 20x6, 12x5 — `>` clipping and row clipping together, boxes intact. Width-only 28x24 and 20x24 for finding 7.
- Damaged sensors via the Debug `debug` command (selective damage, S. R. Sensors), then 72x13/12/11/9 — how I found finding 2.
- Grow-back: 72x9 → 80x24 and 80x13 → 80x24 on the branch, 72x9 → 80x24 on `main` — #88 confirmed identical.
- Startup refusals at 71x24 and 72x12 (classic-display fallback still printed).
- Plain mode: `printf 'regular\nshort\nnovice\nxyz\nsrscan\nquit\nn\n' | ./build/sst` — unchanged.
- `tests/tui.sh` in full against both binaries: branch passes (`tui OK`, exit 0); the branch's suite against the `main` binary fails exactly the four new assertions and nothing else, so the new coverage is real and targeted.

content.text:
## Verdict

The code change is right and I could not break it. The caption now tracks the box's real bottom border at every height I could produce — 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 rows — and the `getmaxy(wquad) >= 2` guard does exactly what it was reasoned to do: at a two-row panel the caption lands on the bottom border below the title, and at a one-row panel it is dropped rather than written over " Quadrant 3 - 2 ". The width guard is untouched by it (caption at 20 columns, gone at 19, at every short height). 80x24 and 72x24 are byte-for-byte identical to a fresh build of `c2fd28b`, with sensors both working and damaged. What still needs changing is the README: the recovery sentence is not true as written, and the fourteen-row sentence is true but sets an expectation the game does not meet. One nit on the new test's precision. **Needs changes** — in `README.md` only.

## Findings

**1. should-fix — `README.md:33-38`, the recovery sentence contradicts itself and blames the wrong axis.**

> "Widening after a narrowing brings the panels straight back, but height is not so forgiving: squeezed under about thirty columns or fourteen rows the display does not recover on its own"

A player is told in one clause that widening always works, and in the next that narrowing under thirty columns does not recover — and a narrowing under thirty columns is precisely the case the first clause promised. It is not a height-versus-width story; I measured it both ways and each axis has a threshold and behaves the same either side of it:

| squeeze, then back to 80x24 | result |
| --- | --- |
| 40 columns | panels fully restored |
| 30 columns | panels fully restored |
| 29 columns | quadrant box stretched a column, right border gone (#88) |
| 14 rows | panels fully restored, `COMMAND>` on row 14 |
| 13 rows | quadrant box stretched to the full screen, no prompt at all |

So "about thirty columns or fourteen rows" is the correct pair of thresholds — that part is well observed — but "height is not so forgiving" is not what distinguishes them. What actually differs is the severity: a bad width leaves a cosmetic border fault and a working prompt; a bad height leaves the player with no prompt. Suggested wording that says only what is true:

> Widening or growing the terminal after a squeeze brings the panels straight back, so long as the squeeze stopped above about thirty columns and fourteen rows. Below either the display does not recover on its own — and below fourteen rows the prompt does not come back with it — so quitting and starting again is the way back.

I did verify the escape hatch the sentence promises: from the wrecked 13-rows-and-back state, typing `quit`, `n`, Enter, `n` blind does reach "May the Great Bird of the Galaxy roost upon your home planet." and exits. The advice holds; it just happens with no visible feedback.

**2. should-fix — `README.md:33-34`, "fourteen rows" reads as a floor that works, and fourteen rows does not work.**

"Shorter than fourteen rows there is no room left for the conversation at all" is literally accurate — at 13 the prompt is off-screen, at 14 `COMMAND>` is on row 14. But the natural reading is that fourteen is the size at which the conversation still functions, and it does not. The pager's page size is `LINES-PANELH-1` (`tui.c:766`), which is 0 at fourteen rows, so at 80x14 `lrscan` produces this and nothing else, page after page:

```
mqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqjmqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqj
 [HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]
```

At 15 rows the pager shows one blank line above itself; at 16 it finally shows one line of scan ("Long-range scan for Quadrant 3 - 2"). Suggest the paragraph admit the approach as well as the cliff, e.g. "...and the prompt is not on it. Just above that there is barely more: at fourteen or fifteen rows the one line left goes to the pager, so a scan pages past with nothing to read." The zero-line pager itself is out of this slice — pre-existing, untouched by the diff, and adjacent to but distinct from #94, which is about *below* fourteen. Worth filing separately (I only report; the main agent files).

**3. nit — `tests/tui.sh:1082-1090`, the new 80x11 check asserts presence, not place.**

It does fail against the pre-fix binary for the right reason (I ran the whole suite against a fresh build of `c2fd28b`: all five new assertions fail, including "sensors: the dashes lost their reason on a short terminal"), so it is a real test. But `expect` is a whole-screen substring search, and the fix is specifically about *which row* the caption lands on. A regression that drew it over a grid row, or over the title, would pass. The sibling block you added ten lines earlier is positional (`NR == h`), and this one could be too — at 80x11 the caption is on screen row 11, so a check that row 11 carries it would hold the fix to what it actually claims and match the surrounding style.

**4. no action — the caption in the unrecovered state.** Worth knowing, since it is a behaviour change your diff causes outside supported sizes: after 13 rows and back to 24, with sensors damaged, the old code left " SENSORS DAMAGED" floating on a blank row 12 inside the stretched box; the new code puts it on that box's real bottom border at row 24, twelve rows below the dashes it explains. Neither is good, the whole display is already wrecked there, and the new one is at least structurally correct (a caption on a border rather than adrift inside a panel). I would not change it.

## What I exercised

All TUI work on my own tmux socket (`-L uirev2`, `-f /dev/null`), killed and its socket file removed at the end; the temporary worktree used for the baseline build was removed and `git worktree list` and `git status --short` are back to just your three modified files. No files edited.

- Started `./build/sst -t tournament 7 short novice pw`, reached `COMMAND>`, damaged the short-range sensors via `debug` (the `n n n y y n...` sequence) and confirmed the caption on the bottom border.

## Verdict

The code change is right and I could not break it. The caption now tracks the box's real bottom border at every height I could produce — 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 rows — and the `getmaxy(wquad) >= 2` guard does exactly what it was reasoned to do: at a two-row panel the caption lands on the bottom border below the title, and at a one-row panel it is dropped rather than written over " Quadrant 3 - 2 ". The width guard is untouched by it (caption at 20 columns, gone at 19, at every short height). 80x24 and 72x24 are byte-for-byte identical to a fresh build of `c2fd28b`, with sensors both working and damaged. What still needs changing is the README: the recovery sentence is not true as written, and the fourteen-row sentence is true but sets an expectation the game does not meet. One nit on the new test's precision. **Needs changes** — in `README.md` only.

## Findings

**1. should-fix — `README.md:33-38`, the recovery sentence contradicts itself and blames the wrong axis.**

> "Widening after a narrowing brings the panels straight back, but height is not so forgiving: squeezed under about thirty columns or fourteen rows the display does not recover on its own"

A player is told in one clause that widening always works, and in the next that narrowing under thirty columns does not recover — and a narrowing under thirty columns is precisely the case the first clause promised. It is not a height-versus-width story; I measured it both ways and each axis has a threshold and behaves the same either side of it:

| squeeze, then back to 80x24 | result |
| --- | --- |
| 40 columns | panels fully restored |
| 30 columns | panels fully restored |
| 29 columns | quadrant box stretched a column, right border gone (#88) |
| 14 rows | panels fully restored, `COMMAND>` on row 14 |
| 13 rows | quadrant box stretched to the full screen, no prompt at all |

So "about thirty columns or fourteen rows" is the correct pair of thresholds — that part is well observed — but "height is not so forgiving" is not what distinguishes them. What actually differs is the severity: a bad width leaves a cosmetic border fault and a working prompt; a bad height leaves the player with no prompt. Suggested wording that says only what is true:

> Widening or growing the terminal after a squeeze brings the panels straight back, so long as the squeeze stopped above about thirty columns and fourteen rows. Below either the display does not recover on its own — and below fourteen rows the prompt does not come back with it — so quitting and starting again is the way back.

I did verify the escape hatch the sentence promises: from the wrecked 13-rows-and-back state, typing `quit`, `n`, Enter, `n` blind does reach "May the Great Bird of the Galaxy roost upon your home planet." and exits. The advice holds; it just happens with no visible feedback.

**2. should-fix — `README.md:33-34`, "fourteen rows" reads as a floor that works, and fourteen rows does not work.**

"Shorter than fourteen rows there is no room left for the conversation at all" is literally accurate — at 13 the prompt is off-screen, at 14 `COMMAND>` is on row 14. But the natural reading is that fourteen is the size at which the conversation still functions, and it does not. The pager's page size is `LINES-PANELH-1` (`tui.c:766`), which is 0 at fourteen rows, so at 80x14 `lrscan` produces this and nothing else, page after page:

```
 [HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]
```

At 15 rows the pager shows one blank line above itself; at 16 it finally shows one line of scan ("Long-range scan for Quadrant 3 - 2"). Suggest the paragraph admit the approach as well as the cliff, e.g. "...and the prompt is not on it. Just above that there is barely more: at fourteen or fifteen rows the one line left goes to the pager, so a scan pages past with nothing to read." The zero-line pager itself is out of this slice — pre-existing, untouched by the diff, and adjacent to but distinct from #94, which is about *below* fourteen. Worth filing separately (I only report; the main agent files).

**3. nit — `tests/tui.sh:1082-1090`, the new 80x11 check asserts presence, not place.**

It does fail against the pre-fix binary for the right reason (I ran the whole suite against a fresh build of `c2fd28b`: all five new assertions fail, including "sensors: the dashes lost their reason on a short terminal"), so it is a real test. But `expect` is a whole-screen substring search, and the fix is specifically about *which row* the caption lands on. A regression that drew it over a grid row, or over the title, would pass. The sibling block you added ten lines earlier is positional (`NR == h`), and this one could be too — at 80x11 the caption is on screen row 11, so a check that row 11 carries it would hold the fix to what it actually claims and match the surrounding style.

**4. no action — the caption in the unrecovered state.** Worth knowing, since it is a behaviour change your diff causes outside supported sizes: after 13 rows and back to 24, with sensors damaged, the old code left " SENSORS DAMAGED" floating on a blank row 12 inside the stretched box; the new code puts it on that box's real bottom border at row 24, twelve rows below the dashes it explains. ## Verdict: **pass**

No failure, flake, or regression found. Everything the brief asked to be checked hardest was reproduced independently, and every measurable README claim was re-measured and holds.

---

## What ran

**Builds** (all clean, no warnings)
- `cmake -S . -B build-debug -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug && cmake --build build-debug` — exit 0
- `cmake -S . -B build-release -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build-release` — exit 0

**Static checks**
- `gcc -std=gnu17 ... -Wall -Wextra -Wmissing-prototypes -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wstrict-prototypes -c tui.c`: 4 warnings, **all four identical on the merge-base `tui.c`** (`tui.c:150`, `:160` shadowed `a`; `:600`, `:724` sign-conversion). None in changed code.
- `gcc -fanalyzer` on `tui.c`: 0 warnings.
- `shellcheck -S style tests/tui.sh`: clean.

**Tests** — `ctest --test-dir build-debug` and `--test-dir build-release`: 11/11 pass at both. `tests/tui.sh ./build-debug/sst Debug` run 4 more times standalone (0 failures, 47.2-47.4 s each) plus once under 24-way CPU load (0 failures) — no flakiness.

**Journeys** — all on my own tmux socket (`-f /dev/null -L verif-*`), never the default; every server I started is dead and my socket files removed. Nothing else on the socket directory touched.

---

## The five things you asked to be checked hardest

**1. Every new assertion, lexed.** All three fire; none is dead.

- `awk -v h="$h" 'NR == h && /[0-9]/ {bad=1} END {exit bad ? 1 : 0}'` — correct (uninitialised `bad` is falsy in mawk → exit 0). I confirmed `capture-pane -p` emits **all** pane rows including trailing blanks (measured: 9 lines from a cleared 9-row pane), so `NR == h` really addresses the last row and cannot pass by truncation. Killed by m1 and m2.
- `NR == 11 && /SENSORS DAMAGED/` — killed by m1 and m3. I also confirmed it is not passing by accident of the #88 residue left by the preceding 19-column squeeze: it lands on row 11 both in the script's actual sequence (box left 30 columns wide) and in a clean 80x24 → 80x11 sequence.
- `grep -qE '^.q? *[0-9]+ .*[^0-9]1?[0-9] +\.'` — the one you trusted least is sound. It matches the real defect line `mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .mqKlingons Left 2...` and matched **0 lines** across every healthy capture I took (72x24, 80x24, 100x30, 29x24, 80x13, sensors damaged, 1-3 row panels). Killed by m1. One brittleness note under *Missing coverage* below.

**2. Mutants re-run, independently built.** Three copies of the working tree (uncommitted test included), `build/` left behind, configured fresh; each `CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` verified to point at itself:

| mutant | failures | which |
|---|---|---|
| `panel_has_row` → `return 1` | **5** | border at 72x12, 72x11, 72x9; two grid rows on one line; caption row |
| `wresize(wstat, PANELH, statw)` | **3** | border at 72x12, 72x11, 72x9 |
| caption row → `PANELH-1` | **1** | caption row |

Exactly your counts. Symptoms are mutation-specific (m2 touches only the status side, m3 only the caption), which is independent evidence the mutated sources reached the binaries.

**3. Nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24.** Byte-for-byte identical to a merge-base build (`c2fd28b` sources, own build tree) across four captured states each — at the prompt, after `srscan`, after `debug`-damaged sensors, and `srscan` with sensors damaged. The damaged states are non-vacuous (`SENSORS DAMAGED` present in both). Plain mode on the seeded journey (`tournament 7 …`) is byte-identical to the merge-base too; the unseeded `regular` journey differs run-to-run on the *same* binary, so that is randomness, not a change.

**4. The `getmaxy(wquad) >= 2` guard.** Independently confirmed at 3, 2 and 1 rows with sensors damaged. Branch: caption on the bottom border at 3 and 2 rows, correctly absent at 1 row, no garbage, process alive, quits cleanly. **5. Builds/suites/plain mode.** Above.

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| recovery threshold "about thirty columns" | 30 columns recovers fully; 29 does not (quadrant box left one column stretched, right border merged). Identical to merge-base at 29 → #88. |

(My first two attempts failed only because I sent bare Spaces to a line-based read; that was my error, not the game's.) |

1. **The new sweep only checks that nothing lands on the border — never that everything that fits is drawn.** I built a fourth mutant, `panel_has_row` with `row < getmaxy(w) - 3` (clips two rows too many). input.content:
fix(tui): clip the panels by row as well as by column

#78 bounded the panel draw loops by column. Nothing bounded them by
row, and tui_refresh_panels() asks for all eleven lines however short
the terminal is. Two ways to fail, one on each side of the last row: at
twelve rows the tenth grid line was drawn onto the bottom border, and
at eleven wmove() failed outright, left the cursor where the previous
line had left it, and the whole line landed on the row above --
`mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .x`, two grid rows and a border sharing
one line.

panel_has_row() asks what panel_room() asks on the other axis, and both
draw loops return early when the row is not inside the box. That alone
fixed the quadrant panel and not the status panel, which turned out to
be a second defect: make_windows() resized the status panel back to its
full PANELH rows on every repaint whatever the screen height, so it
stayed taller than the screen, its bottom border fell off the bottom,
and its last line was drawn where that border should have been. It now
takes the height the screen can show, as the quadrant panel already did
by way of resize_term().

A third, found by ui-review: the SENSORS DAMAGED caption still named
row PANELH-1 absolutely, so from twelve rows down the dashes lost their
explanation entirely -- the field of nothing with no reason given that
the caption exists to prevent, at the sizes where a player is least
sure what they are looking at. It now asks the window where its bottom
border is.

Rows clip in silence, unlike the columns #78 marked with `>`. A
truncated number is a plausible wrong number and needed the marker; a
dropped row leaves nothing to misread, the grid keeps its numbering so
the stopping point is legible, and every height at which a row drops is
already a height with no prompt on screen (#94). They go from the
bottom, which costs Klingons Left and Time Left first -- reordering the
panel under pressure would change the field order as a player drags,
and tuifmt.c mirrors srscan(), which is the spec.

Nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24, byte-for-byte against the merge-base
with sensors working and damaged.

Each of the three parts has an assertion that dies without it, proven
by mutants built in copies outside the repository with
CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY checked. Two of the new assertions did not say
what they appeared to and were caught by review: one leaned on this
seed's quadrant having a dot in a particular cell, and now keys on the
label spacing that tells a grid row from the column header; the other
was a positive control that the defect it guarded could erase, so a
relaxed guard failed the control and never reached the line naming the
defect.

Filed, not fixed: #88, #90, and two found here -- #94, no prompt at all
below fourteen rows, which this change makes more visible rather than
less by leaving a tidy display that never responds; and #95, the pager
having no lines to show at fourteen.

Closes #91

gh pr create --title "fix(tui): clip the panels by row as well as by column" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes #91.

## The bug

The change that closed #78 bounded the panel draw loops by **column**.
Nothing bounded them by **row**, and `tui_refresh_panels()` asks for all
eleven lines however short the terminal is. Two ways to fail, one on
each side of the last row:

- At **12 rows** the tenth grid line was drawn *onto* the bottom border
  — in bounds, wrong row.
- At **11** `wmove` failed outright, left the cursor where the previous
  line had left it, and the whole line landed on the row above:

```
mq 9  . . . . . . . . . .10 .x Klingons Left 2
```

Two grid rows and a border sharing one line.

## The fix has three parts, and only the first was anticipated

1. **`panel_has_row()`** — the question `panel_room()` asks on the other
   axis — and an early return in both draw loops.
2. **`make_windows()` was resizing the status panel back to `PANELH`
   rows on every repaint** regardless of screen height, so it stayed
   taller than the screen, its bottom border fell off the bottom, and
   its last line was drawn where that border should have been. Found
   only because part 1 alone fixed the quadrant panel and not the
   status panel.
3. **The `SENSORS DAMAGED` caption still named row `PANELH-1`
   absolutely**, so from 12 rows down the dashes lost their explanation
   — the field of nothing with no reason given that the caption exists
   to prevent. Found by `ui-review`. It now asks the window where its
   bottom border is.

**Nothing changes at 72x24 or 80x24** — byte-for-byte against the
merge-base with sensors working and damaged.

## Judgment calls, made by review rather than by me

**Rows clip in silence**, unlike the columns #78 marked with `>`. A
truncated number is a plausible wrong number and needed the marker; a
dropped row leaves nothing to misread, the grid keeps its numbering so
the stopping point is legible, and every height at which a row drops is
already a height with no prompt on screen (#94).

**They go from the bottom**, which costs Klingons Left and Time Left
first. Reordering under pressure would change the panel's field order as
a player drags, and `tuifmt.c` mirrors `srscan()`, which is the spec.

## Tests, and four assertions that lied

Each of the three parts has an assertion that dies without it, proven by
mutants built in copies **outside** the repository with
`CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` checked.

Four assertions in this work read convincingly and did not do what they
said. Each was caught by review, not by me:

1. an awk regex written `/></`, which lexes as the regex `><` (on the
   #78 branch)
2. a pattern leaning on this seed's quadrant having a `.` in one cell —
   now keyed on the label spacing that separates a grid row from the
   column header
3. a positive control the defect it guarded could **erase**, so a broken
   build failed the control and never reached the line naming the defect
4. `Time Left`, behind an `elif` that every mutant short-circuited past,
   so nobody had ever seen it fail

The lesson is in the file rather than in a review thread: a mutant that
breaks several assertions at once proves the first branch and hides the
rest, so three of these needed a mutant built to isolate them.

## Issues

Left open, and filed: #88, #90, and two found here —

- **#94** — below fourteen rows there is no conversation and no prompt.
  This change makes it *more* visible, not less: the display is now
  tidy and simply never responds.
- **#95** — at fourteen rows the pager has no lines to show. Its body
  was corrected by comment after a second measurement showed fifteen
  rows pages one line at a time rather than nothing.

## Verification

`ui-review` twice — the second round because part 3 changes what the
game draws. `verifier` once, pass. `code-review` across four rounds on
this branch, the last re-running every mutant against the final test
file. The README's four numeric claims — the fourteen-row conversation
cliff, the fourteen-row pager, fifteen paging one line at a time, and
the fourteen-row recovery boundary — were measured against the running
game three times, and corrected twice.

Builds clean at both types with `-DSST_WERROR=ON`; `ctest` 11/11 at
both; plain mode byte-identical on a deterministic seed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

---
description: Run a Codex review that challenges the implementation approach and design choices
argument-hint: '[--wait|--background] [--base <ref>] [--scope auto|working-tree|branch] [focus ...]'
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash(node:*), Bash(git:*), AskUserQuestion
---

Run an adversarial Codex review through the shared plugin runtime.
Position it as a challenge review that questions the chosen implementation, design choices, tradeoffs, and assumptions.
It is not just a stricter pass over implementation defects.

Raw slash-command arguments:
`$ARGUMENTS`

Core constraint:
- This command is review-only.
- Do not fix issues, apply patches, or suggest that you are about to make changes.
- Your only job is to run the review and return Codex's output verbatim to the user.
- Keep the framing focused on whether the current approach is the right one, what assumptions it depends on, and where the design could fail under real-world conditions.

Execution mode rules:
- If the raw arguments include `--wait`, do not ask. Run in the foreground.
- If the raw arguments include `--background`, do not ask. Run in a Claude background task.
- Otherwise, estimate the review size before asking:
  - For working-tree review, start with `git status --short --untracked-files=all`.
  - For working-tree review, also inspect both `git diff --shortstat --cached` and `git diff --shortstat`.
  - For base-branch review, use `git diff --shortstat <base>...HEAD`.
  - Treat untracked files or directories as reviewable work for auto or working-tree review even when `git diff --shortstat` is empty.
  - Only conclude there is nothing to review when the relevant scope is actually empty.
  - Recommend waiting only when the scoped review is clearly tiny, roughly 1-2 files total and no sign of a broader directory-sized change.
  - In every other case, including unclear size, recommend background.
  - When in doubt, run the review instead of declaring that there is nothing to review.
- Then use `AskUserQuestion` exactly once with two options, putting the recommended option first and suffixing its label with `(Recommended)`:
  - `Wait for results`
  - `Run in background`

Argument handling:
- Preserve the user's arguments exactly.
- Do not strip `--wait` or `--background` yourself.
- Do not weaken the adversarial framing or rewrite the user's focus text.
- The companion script parses `--wait` and `--background`, but Claude Code's `Bash(..., run_in_background: true)` is what actually detaches the run.
- `/codex:adversarial-review` uses the same review target selection as `/codex:review`.
- It supports working-tree review, branch review, and `--base <ref>`.
- It does not support `--scope staged` or `--scope unstaged`.
- Unlike `/codex:review`, it can still take extra focus text after the flags.

Foreground flow:
- Run:
```bash
node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" adversarial-review "$ARGUMENTS"
```
- Return the command stdout verbatim, exactly as-is.
- Do not paraphrase, summarize, or add commentary before or after it.
- Do not fix any issues mentioned in the review output.

Background flow:
- Launch the review with `Bash` in the background:
```typescript
Bash({
  command: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/codex-companion.mjs" adversarial-review "$ARGUMENTS"`,
  description: "Codex adversarial review",
  run_in_background: true
})
```
- Do not call `BashOutput` or wait for completion in this turn.
- After launching the command, tell the user: "Codex adversarial review started in the background. Check `/codex:status` for progress."

content.text:
Two things about `/codex:adversarial-review` change what the workflow can say, so let me settle them before editing AGENTS.md.

**It cannot be invoked by an agent.** Its frontmatter sets `disable-model-invocation: true` — which is why it's absent from my skills list while `codex:rescue` and `codex:setup` appear. Only a human typing `/codex:adversarial-review` can start it. The underlying runtime (`codex-companion.mjs`) is reachable from Bash, but going that way deliberately bypasses the gate the plugin author put there, including its own wait-vs-background prompt.

The rest checks out: `codex-cli 0.147.0` is on PATH, the review is explicitly review-only ("Do not fix issues, apply patches"), it takes focus text, and it returns a structured `approve` / `needs-attention` verdict with severity-ranked findings — which fits step 8's gate cleanly.

### The review sub-agents

Steps 6-8 invoke Claude Code sub-agents defined in `.claude/agents/`:
`ui-review`, `verifier` and `code-review`. What matters is not the tool. It
is that the work is judged by a reader who did not write it, and who
reaches its conclusions from the diff rather than from a memory of having
intended something.

Which of the three bind depends on what changed. `code-review` binds on
every commit, without exception — it is the gate step 8 describes.
`verifier` binds as well, with the scope step 7 already gives it: the
checks appropriate for the change, which for a file nothing compiles can
come down to a single test — the sub-agent still runs, even when what it
has to run is one test. `ui-review` binds when the change can alter what
the game shows a player or asks of them. This file, a test's plumbing and
CI configuration usually give it nothing to read; the build system does
the moment it changes what gets compiled in, since `-DSCORE`, `-DCAPTURE`,
`-DCLOAKING` and the `-DDEBUG` that Debug builds add all decide which
commands and messages the game has at all.

When it is unclear whether a change reaches the player, run the pass. A
`ui-review` with nothing to say costs one pass; code that runs while the
game runs reaches the player whether the change meant it to or not, and a
refactor that preserves behavior is exactly where a lost line hides.

Skipping it is a decision, not an omission. Say that it was skipped and
why — to `code-review` when invoking it, per step 8, and in the commit,
the pull request body and the summary of the work. The last three put it
on the record; the first is the one that reaches a reviewer with a
mandate to argue back, and reaches it before there is a commit to argue
about, which is why step 8 asks for it as well. An agent writing that
sentence about a change to the game's own output has skipped the wrong
pass.

`/codex:adversarial-review` is step 8's second pass. It runs the Codex
CLI against the working tree or the branch and returns a verdict of

It is not a stricter `code-review`, and swapping one for the other
loses something either way. Its prompt tells it to report only material
findings and to leave style, naming and cleanup alone, and its attack
surface is written for services — trust boundaries, data loss, retries,
partial failure, schema drift. Nothing in it knows that `sst.doc` is the
specification, that the golden recordings are the only check on the
game's arithmetic, that plain mode must not change as a side effect, or
that `ui-review` was owed and skipped. Those live in
`.claude/agents/code-review.md` and stay there. So say what to attack
when you ask for the review, in the terms this game has: the rule in
`sst.doc` the change claims to implement, the journey a player takes
through it, the state the change assumes the galaxy is in.

`disable-model-invocation`, which is why it does not appear to an agent
as something it can invoke, and why step 8 has the agent stop and ask
rather than run it. Reaching the same runtime through `node
.../codex-companion.mjs` would defeat both the author's decision and the
prompt that asks whether to wait or run in the background, and it names

working tree, which is the default; after one, `--scope branch` or
`--base main` is the diff a reviewer of the pull request would see.

no Codex CLI, a harness that has no slash commands at all — that is a
fact to report, in the same sentence that reports which of the other
passes ran, and in the commit, the pull request body and the summary of
the work. It is not a reason to stop: `code-review` is the gate and it
still binds. But a reader told that the change was reviewed should not
have to guess how many reviewers that means."""

# Verdict: **fail**

One claim in the new prose is false, and I can reproduce the failing case deterministically. Everything you asked me to check about `.claude/settings.json` is clean.

## 1. `.claude/settings.json` — clean, checked from the outside
